docs.text:
The primary return type of create_tutorial_flow() is an instance of pocketflow.Flow.

Field / Attribute Type Description start BaseNode The designated entry node of the DAG (fetch_repo). run Callable[[dict], None] Orchestration method that receives the shared dictionary and walks the DAG until all terminal nodes complete.

docs.title: Pipeline Shared Store Context Contract
docs.text:
Although flow.py does not directly manipulate the shared state dictionary, it defines the graph edges that pass this state between nodes. The table below outlines the core schema expectations of the shared dictionary as it moves through the configured nodes:

Key Expected Type Producer Node Consumer Node(s) Description repo_path str Entry (main.py) FetchRepo Filesystem path or remote URL of the target codebase. files_data list[tuple[str, str]] FetchRepo ContextRouter, All Mappers List of (relative_path, file_content) tuples extracted during crawl. directory_tree str FetchRepo ContextRouter, All Mappers Serialized text representation of the repository directory layout. context_mode str ContextRouter PocketFlow Routing Engine Resolved routing action: "direct", "batch", or "deterministic". abstractions list[dict] IdentifyAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions AnalyzeRelationships Extracted core architectural concepts and their source mappings. relationships list[dict] AnalyzeRelationships OrderChapters Cross-concept dependency and interaction definitions. chapters list[dict] OrderChapters, DeterministicFileMapper WriteChapters Ordered curriculum structure defining chapter titles, paths, and contents. written_chapters list[dict] WriteChapters CombineTutorial Synthesized Markdown chapter payloads with summary briefs. final_output_dir str CombineTutorial Exit (main.py) Destination path containing the rendered MkDocs site or standalone Markdown files.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The flow.py module establishes error resilience through declarative node configuration and graph design rather than explicit try/except blocks:

  • Inference Rate Limiting & Transient Network Faults: Remote LLM calls are vulnerable to network interruptions and provider throttling. Every node interacting with remote inference APIs (MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions, IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships, OrderChapters, WriteChapters, DeterministicFileMapper) is instantiated with max_retries=5 and wait=20. If an underlying call to call_llm() fails, PocketFlow catches the failure, blocks for 20 seconds, and retries up to five times before marking the node as failed.
  • Graph Path Isolation: Conditional routing guarantees path isolation. By segregating "direct", "batch", and "deterministic" paths at ContextRouter, the pipeline prevents incompatible processing states from executing simultaneously. For example, MapAbstractions will never run if ContextRouter selects "direct", preventing unneeded chunking overhead.
  • Deterministic Fallback Convergence: The "deterministic" route bypasses both abstraction analysis (IdentifyAbstractions / ReduceAbstractions) and relationship mapping (AnalyzeRelationships), feeding its outputs directly into WriteChapters. This ensures that even if a codebase cannot be processed via abstraction extraction, the graph can still converge at WriteChapters and complete document synthesis.
  • Flow-Level Failure Propagation: PocketFlow terminates execution and bubbles exceptions to the runtime caller (main.py) if any node exhausts its configured retry attempts. Unhandled failures inside local nodes (FetchRepo, ContextRouter, CombineTutorial) fail immediately without retries, surfacing bugs in file I/O or configuration without masking them.

Source: main.py

Following the workflow DAG configuration and node connectivity patterns established in flow.py, the main.py module serves as the primary command-line interface (CLI) entry point and system lifecycle orchestrator for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder architecture. It exposes an executable command-line contract, parses and normalizes user runtime parameters, manages environment variable loading, validates option compatibility, constructs the centralized execution state, and drives the pipeline graph through its full execution lifecycle to final resource teardown.

The module operates as the boundary adapter between the external operating environment and internal workflow engines. Upon execution, it initializes system-wide terminal telemetry, loads runtime secrets from .env files, detects underlying Large Language Model (LLM) provider infrastructure, inspects and enforces context window token ceilings, and builds the primary SharedStoreContext dictionary that is passed across PocketFlow execution nodes. docs.title: main()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def main() -> None:

Description: Acts as the master orchestrator and runtime lifecycle manager for the entire application. It executes in five distinct operational phases: parsing arguments and bootstrapping the localized output system; validating ingestion targets and standalone maintenance tasks; resolving project naming and enforcing caching invariants; assembling the PocketFlow shared state and initializing logging; and dispatching the directed acyclic graph (DAG) inside a try...finally block to ensure all file sinks and stream buffers are flushed via shutdown().

docs.title: CLI Initialization and Quoting Verification
docs.text:
parser, args = parse_arguments()
    init_output(
        language=args.language,
        use_cache=not args.no_cache,
        thinking_level=args.thinking_level,
        debug=args.debug,
    )
    _check_quoting_errors(parser, args)

    # Handle standalone --cleanup (no --dir or --repo)
    if args.cleanup and not args.dir and not args.repo:
        _run_cleanup()
        return
This phase begins by executing parse_arguments() to bind CLI flags to an argparse.Namespace object. It then invokes init_output() from utils/output.py to set up localized string tables, cache states, reasoning effort levels, and terminal debugging output. Next, it passes the parser and namespace to _check_quoting_errors() to catch CLI quoting corruptions before they propagate. If the invocation specifies the --cleanup flag without a repository URL or local directory, it executes _run_cleanup() and terminates the process immediately.

docs.title: Ingestion Target and Credential Resolution
docs.text:
# Require --dir or --repo for generation
    if not args.dir and not args.repo:
        parser.error("one of the arguments --repo --dir --cleanup is required")

    # Get GitHub token from argument or environment variable if using repo
    github_token = None
    if args.repo:
        github_token = args.token or os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN")
        if not github_token:
            emit("WARN_NO_GITHUB_TOKEN")
    elif args.token:
        emit("WARN_TOKEN_NO_REPO")

    mode, project_name = resolve_mode_and_project(args)
This phase enforces that at least one ingestion target (--repo or --dir) is provided when not performing a standalone cleanup, halting execution with parser.error if neither is present. If analyzing a remote repository, it extracts the GitHub authentication token from either the CLI --token argument or the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable, emitting WARN_NO_GITHUB_TOKEN if credentials cannot be resolved. Conversely, if a token was supplied for a local directory analysis, it issues WARN_TOKEN_NO_REPO. Finally, it calls resolve_mode_and_project() to determine the documentation style and target project name.

docs.title: Documentation Mode and Incremental Cache Verification
docs.text:
# Enforce incremental cache constraints
    if args.incremental and mode != "api-reference":
        emit("WARN_INCREMENTAL_API_ONLY")
        args.incremental = False

    # --force-rebuild requires --incremental
    if args.force_rebuild and not args.incremental:
        emit("ERROR_FORCE_REBUILD_NO_INCREMENTAL")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Handle --force-rebuild: delete the cache manifest to force fresh generation
    if args.force_rebuild and args.incremental:
        output_base = args.output or "output"
        manifest_path = os.path.join(output_base, project_name, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
        if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
            os.remove(manifest_path)
            emit("FORCE_REBUILD_DELETED", path=manifest_path)
        else:
            emit("FORCE_REBUILD_NO_MANIFEST", path=manifest_path)

    # Warn about args ignored in api-reference mode
    if mode == "api-reference" and args.force_batch:
        emit("WARN_FORCE_BATCH_API_REF")
        args.force_batch = False
This phase validates documentation mode flags, restricting --incremental caching exclusively to the api-reference mode and disabling it with a warning if supplied under other modes. It requires --force-rebuild to be coupled with --incremental, calling sys.exit(1) if this invariant is violated. When a valid forced rebuild is detected, the manifest file (.doc_cache_manifest.json) in the project output directory is purged to ensure clean generation. Lastly, it turns off --force-batch with a warning if api-reference mode is active, as that mode uses a deterministic file mapping pipeline instead of map-reduce batching.

docs.title: Context Assembly, Logging, and Pre-Flight Display
docs.text:
shared = build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode)
    provider, model_name, endpoint_url, _, context_length = detect_llm_config(args)
    log_file = configure_logging(project_name=project_name, mode=mode)
    display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file)
This phase aggregates parsed parameters, exclusion sets, and pipeline state into the master shared context store via build_shared_store(). It calls detect_llm_config() to detect active LLM providers, model identifiers, API base endpoints, and context window limits. It then registers the session's disk logger by calling configure_logging() in utils/output.py. Finally, it calls display_config() to output a pre-flight summary of the execution environment, model parameters, and operational flags to standard output.

docs.title: Graph Flow Execution and Resource Teardown
docs.text:
# Create and run the flow
    tutorial_flow = create_tutorial_flow()
    try:
        tutorial_flow.run(shared)

        # Cleanup after run if requested
        if args.cleanup:
            _run_cleanup()
    finally:
        from utils.output import shutdown

        shutdown()
This phase instantiates the pipeline graph by calling create_tutorial_flow() from flow.py. It executes the workflow inside a try block via tutorial_flow.run(shared), dispatching downstream node operations across ingestion, abstraction, relationship analysis, and chapter synthesis. If the --cleanup flag was set alongside an ingestion target, post-execution cleanup runs via _run_cleanup(). Regardless of whether pipeline execution succeeds or throws an unhandled exception, the finally block imports and executes shutdown() to flush file buffers and release logging handlers.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * SystemExit: Raised with code 1 if --force-rebuild is supplied without --incremental, or if shell quoting errors are detected. * argparse.ArgumentError: Raised via parser.error() if neither --dir, --repo, nor --cleanup is supplied.

Example: 

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: parse_arguments()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_arguments() -> tuple[argparse.ArgumentParser, argparse.Namespace]:

Description: Constructs the command-line argument parser, registers the flag definitions, constraints, defaults, and help strings, and parses arguments from sys.argv.

docs.title: Source Ingestion and File Filter Flag Setup
docs.text:
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Generate a tutorial for a GitHub codebase or local directory.")

    # Source: --repo or --dir (mutually exclusive but not required if --cleanup is used)
    source_group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    source_group.add_argument("--repo", help="URL of the public GitHub repository.")
    source_group.add_argument("--dir", help="Path to local directory.")
    parser.add_argument("--cleanup", action="store_true", help="Clean up logs and cache files. Can be used standalone or after a run.")

    parser.add_argument("-n", "--name", help="Project name (optional, derived from repo/directory if omitted).")
    parser.add_argument("-t", "--token", help="GitHub personal access token (optional, reads from GITHUB_TOKEN env var if not provided).")
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", default="output", help="Base directory for output (default: ./output).")
    parser.add_argument("-i", "--include", nargs="+", help="Files to include (e.g., '*.py' '*.js'). Defaults to '*' (all files).")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-e",
        "--exclude",
        nargs="+",
        help="Files to exclude. Custom patterns are automatically merged with a massive global exclusion list (build caches, node_modules, binaries, media, AI environments) AND your repository's native .gitignore rules.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("-s", "--max-size", type=int, default=200000, help="Maximum file size in bytes (default: 200000, about 200KB).")
This phase configures the core ingestion options. A mutually exclusive group ensures that --repo and --dir cannot be supplied simultaneously, while allowing both to be omitted when running standalone --cleanup. It registers inclusion (-i/--include) and exclusion (-e/--exclude) pattern lists using nargs="+", along with parameters for the project output directory (-o/--output), GitHub personal access token (-t/--token), project name override (-n/--name), and individual file byte limits (-s/--max-size).

docs.title: Model Reasoning, Execution Mode, and Pipeline Control Flag Setup
docs.text:
# Add language parameter for multi-language support
    parser.add_argument("--language", default="english", help="Language for the generated tutorial (default: english).")
    # Add use_cache parameter to control LLM caching
    parser.add_argument("--no-cache", action="store_true", help="Disable LLM response caching (default: caching enabled).")
    # Add max_abstraction_num parameter to control the number of abstractions
    parser.add_argument("--max-abstractions", type=int, default=10, help="Maximum number of abstractions to identify (default: 10).")
    # Add thinking_level parameter for LLM reasoning capabilities
    parser.add_argument(
        "--thinking-level",
        default=None,
        help="Thinking effort level for native Gemini, OpenRouter, and Ollama reasoning models (e.g., low, medium, high). Leave empty to use model defaults.",
    )
    # Add max_tokens parameter
    parser.add_argument(
        "--max-tokens", type=int, default=None, help="Maximum number of tokens for the context window (default: fetched dynamically)."
    )

    # --- Documentation Mode & Generation Styles ---
    parser.add_argument(
        "--mode",
        choices=["tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", "sdk"],
        default="tutorial",
        help="Documentation style (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk). (default: tutorial).",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--advanced", action="store_true", help="Legacy flag: equivalent to --mode advanced.")
    parser.add_argument("--mkdocs", action="store_true", help="Format output for MkDocs Material (adds YAML frontmatter & nav snippet).")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--incremental",
        action="store_true",
        help="Enable MD5 incremental caching to skip unchanged modules (Only supported in --mode api-reference).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--force-rebuild", action="store_true", help="Clear incremental cache and regenerate all chapters from scratch (use with --incremental)."
    )

    # Add batching parameters
    parser.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=50, help="Maximum files per batch when using map-reduce mode (default: 50).")
    parser.add_argument("--force-batch", action="store_true", help="Force map-reduce mode regardless of context size.")
    # Debug mode
    parser.add_argument("--debug", action="store_true", help="Enable verbose debug output.")

    return parser, parser.parse_args()
This phase registers flags governing documentation generation styles, reasoning constraints, and execution flow. It defines documentation generation styles (--mode with options tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk), along with the legacy --advanced alias, --mkdocs formatting, and incremental compilation controls (--incremental, --force-rebuild). For the inference layer, it adds arguments for reasoning effort (--thinking-level), context window ceilings (--max-tokens), output language (--language), caching bypass (--no-cache), and maximum abstraction limits (--max-abstractions). Finally, it configures map-reduce batch sizes (--batch), forced batching (--force-batch), and debug logging (--debug), returning both the parser and the resolved Namespace.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * tuple[argparse.ArgumentParser, argparse.Namespace]: A 2-tuple containing the configured ArgumentParser instance and the parsed CLI Namespace.

Raises: * SystemExit: Automatically raised by argparse when CLI validation fails or --help is passed.

Example: 

parser, args = parse_arguments()

docs.title: resolve_mode_and_project()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def resolve_mode_and_project(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[str, str]:

Description: Normalizes the documentation generation mode and derives the target project name. It resolves the legacy --advanced flag against --mode, issuing a warning via WARN_ADVANCED_OVERRIDES_MODE if an explicit --mode was specified alongside --advanced. It then derives a project name if none was passed via -n/--name, extracting the directory basename from os.path.abspath(args.dir) for local directories, parsing the trailing URI segment for remote git repositories, or falling back to "project".

def resolve_mode_and_project(args):
    """Resolve documentation mode (handling --advanced legacy flag) and derive project name.

    Returns:
        tuple[str, str]: (mode, project_name)
    """
    if args.advanced:
        if args.mode != "tutorial":  # User explicitly set --mode AND --advanced
            emit("WARN_ADVANCED_OVERRIDES_MODE", mode=args.mode)
        mode = "advanced"
    else:
        mode = args.mode
    project_name = args.name
    if not project_name:
        if args.dir:
            project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(args.dir))
        elif args.repo:
            project_name = args.repo.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1]
        else:
            project_name = "project"
    return mode, project_name
The function checks args.advanced first to support backward compatibility. When set, it overrides args.mode with "advanced", alerting the user if they also passed a conflicting --mode. Project name derivation handles trailing slashes in remote URLs using .rstrip("/").split("/")[-1], while local directory paths are normalized with os.path.abspath before extracting os.path.basename.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): The parsed command-line argument namespace.

Returns: * tuple[str, str]: A 2-tuple containing the resolved documentation mode (e.g., "tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", "sdk") and the resolved project_name.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

mode, project_name = resolve_mode_and_project(args)

docs.title: build_shared_store()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_shared_store(args: argparse.Namespace, github_token: str | None, mode: str) -> dict[str, any]:

Description: Assembles the central state dictionary shared between PocketFlow nodes. It maps parsed command-line arguments to internal configuration keys, merges user-defined file inclusion and exclusion patterns with system defaults, sets operational flags, and initializes empty collection containers (files, abstractions, relationships, chapter_order, chapters) that downstream pipeline nodes populate during execution.

def build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode):
    """Construct the shared store dictionary passed between PocketFlow nodes.

    Returns:
        dict: The shared store with all CLI args, patterns, and empty output slots.
    """
    return {
        "repo_url": args.repo,
        "local_dir": args.dir,
        "project_name": args.name,  # Can be None, FetchRepo will derive it
        "github_token": github_token,
        "output_dir": args.output,  # Base directory for CombineTutorial output
        # Include/exclude patterns and max file size
        "include_patterns": set(args.include) if args.include else DEFAULT_INCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "exclude_patterns": DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS.union(set(args.exclude)) if args.exclude else DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "max_file_size": args.max_size,
        # Language for multi-language support
        "language": args.language,
        # Cache flag (inverse of no-cache)
        "use_cache": not args.no_cache,
        # Max abstractions
        "max_abstraction_num": args.max_abstractions,
        # LLM reasoning capabilities
        "thinking_level": args.thinking_level,
        # Max tokens override
        "max_tokens": args.max_tokens,
        # Mode, mkdocs, and incremental
        "mode": mode,
        "mkdocs": args.mkdocs,
        "incremental": args.incremental,
        "advanced_mode": mode == "advanced",
        # Batching settings
        "batch_size": args.batch,
        "force_batch": args.force_batch,
        # Debug mode
        "debug": args.debug,
        # Outputs populated by downstream nodes
        "files": [],
        "abstractions": [],
        "relationships": {},
        "chapter_order": [],
        "chapters": [],
        "final_output_dir": None,
    }
The constructor performs pattern set arithmetic, joining user exclusion lists with DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS from utils/exclude_patterns.py using .union(). If --include is omitted, it falls back to DEFAULT_INCLUDE_PATTERNS ({"*"}). It inverts --no-cache into the boolean use_cache, sets advanced_mode to True when mode == "advanced", and pre-allocates empty data structures so pipeline nodes can safely mutate store keys without raising KeyError exceptions.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed command-line argument values. * github_token (str | None): The resolved GitHub personal access token, or None if unauthenticated. * mode (str): The documentation generation mode resolved by resolve_mode_and_project().

Returns: * dict[str, any]: The initialized PocketFlow shared store dictionary.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

shared = build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode)

docs.title: detect_llm_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def detect_llm_config(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[str, str, str, str, int]:

Description: Inspects runtime environment variables to detect active LLM provider configurations and determine context window capacity ceilings. It checks LLM_PROVIDER first, dynamically resolving model names, API endpoints, and authentication keys using the {provider}_* naming convention. If LLM_PROVIDER is missing, it falls back to Google Gemini if either GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY is present. If no recognized provider is found, it defaults to "UNKNOWN". Finally, it sets the context ceiling, using args.max_tokens if explicitly passed, or querying get_model_context_length() from utils/llm_config.py.

def detect_llm_config(args):
    """Detect LLM provider, model, endpoint, and context length from environment.

    Returns:
        tuple: (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length)
    """
    from utils.llm_config import get_model_context_length

    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if provider:
        model_name = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_MODEL", "unknown")
        endpoint_url = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_BASE_URL", "unknown")
        api_key = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_API_KEY", "")
    else:
        # Fallback to Gemini if neither provider is explicitly set but it's used
        if os.environ.get("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") or os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
            provider = "GEMINI"
            model_name = os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.7-flash")
            endpoint_url = "generativelanguage.googleapis.com"
            api_key = os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY", "")
        else:
            provider = "UNKNOWN"
            model_name = "unknown"
            endpoint_url = "unknown"
            api_key = ""

    context_length = args.max_tokens or get_model_context_length(endpoint_url, model_name, api_key)
    return provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length
The function uses a lazy import of get_model_context_length to prevent circular dependencies during module loading. It queries environment variables using standard fallback patterns, defaulting Gemini endpoints to generativelanguage.googleapis.com and models to gemini-3.7-flash. When evaluating token ceilings, args.max_tokens takes precedence over catalog lookups, giving users manual control over context windows when using undocumented or local models.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Command-line arguments containing potential token ceiling overrides (args.max_tokens).

Returns: * tuple[str, str, str, str, int]: A 5-tuple containing: 1. provider (str): Resolved provider name (e.g., "OPENROUTER", "GEMINI", "UNKNOWN"). 2. model_name (str): Configured model identifier string. 3. endpoint_url (str): Model provider API endpoint base URL. 4. api_key (str): API key used for upstream authentication. 5. context_length (int): Maximum context window size in tokens.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

provider, model_name, endpoint_url, _, context_length = detect_llm_config(args)

docs.title: display_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def display_config(args: argparse.Namespace, mode: str, provider: str, model_name: str, endpoint_url: str, context_length: int, log_file: str) -> None:

Description: Emits a formatted summary of the active runtime configuration to the console before pipeline execution begins. It uses emit() and get() from utils/output.py to format and output configuration parameters, applying localization keys for settings such as enabled/disabled states and documentation modes.

def display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file):
    """Emit all configuration values to the console."""
    emit("START_GENERATION", source=args.repo or args.dir, language=args.language.capitalize())
    emit("CFG_HEADER")
    emit("CFG_AI_PROVIDER", value=provider)
    emit("CFG_AI_ENDPOINT", value=endpoint_url)
    emit("CFG_AI_MODEL", value=model_name)
    emit("CFG_CONTEXT_LENGTH", value=f"{context_length:,}")
    emit("CFG_THINKING_LEVEL", value=args.thinking_level or "None")
    emit("CFG_BATCH_SIZE", value=f"{args.batch}")
    _enabled = get("CFG_VALUE_ENABLED")
    _disabled = get("CFG_VALUE_DISABLED")
    emit("CFG_FORCE_BATCH", value=_enabled if args.force_batch else _disabled)
    emit("CFG_OUTPUT_MODE", value=mode)
    emit("CFG_MKDOCS", value=_enabled if args.mkdocs else _disabled)
    emit("CFG_INCREMENTAL", value=_enabled if args.incremental else _disabled)
    if args.incremental:
        emit("CFG_FORCE_REBUILD", value=_enabled if args.force_rebuild else _disabled)
    if mode == "api-reference":
        emit("CFG_MAX_ABSTRACTIONS", value=get("CFG_VALUE_API_REF_MAX"))
    else:
        emit("CFG_MAX_ABSTRACTIONS", value=str(args.max_abstractions))
    emit("CFG_LLM_CACHING", value=_disabled if args.no_cache else _enabled)
    if args.debug:
        emit("CFG_DEBUG_MODE")
    emit("CFG_LOG_FILE", value=log_file)
    print()  # Blank line after config block
The output format presents configuration values consistently using localized string templates. Numbers such as context_length are formatted with thousands separators ({context_length:,}), while boolean states are resolved using localized label keys (CFG_VALUE_ENABLED, CFG_VALUE_DISABLED). If mode is set to "api-reference", abstraction limits are overridden with the localized CFG_VALUE_API_REF_MAX message, reflecting that abstraction discovery is bypassed in that mode.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Command-line arguments. * mode (str): Resolved documentation generation mode. * provider (str): LLM provider identifier. * model_name (str): LLM model name. * endpoint_url (str): API endpoint URL. * context_length (int): Maximum context token capacity. * log_file (str): File path of the active session log.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file)

docs.title: _check_quoting_errors()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _check_quoting_errors(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser, args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:

Description: Identifies shell quoting errors where malformed user input caused --exclude or --include arguments to swallow subsequent CLI flags. This occurs when quotes are misplaced (such as --exclude "dir/* "other/*" --language Vietnamese), causing the shell to group following options into pattern values and leading argparse to silently ignore intended settings. The function extracts registered CLI flags dynamically from parser._actions and checks whether pattern strings contain embedded option flags, calling sys.exit(1) with diagnostic context if corruption is detected.

def _check_quoting_errors(parser, args):
    """Detect shell quoting errors where --exclude/--include values accidentally swallowed other CLI flags.

    When users misquote patterns (e.g., --exclude "autogen/* "SmartFO/*" --language Vietnamese),
    the shell merges subsequent flags into the pattern value. This silently causes ALL following
    arguments to be ignored. We detect this by checking if any pattern value contains a known
    CLI flag string, which no legitimate file/directory pattern would ever contain.

    Flags are extracted dynamically from the argparse parser — no hardcoded list to maintain.
    """
    # Extract all registered flags (both --long and -short) from the parser
    known_flags = set()
    for action in parser._actions:
        for opt in action.option_strings:
            known_flags.add(opt)

    for pattern_list, flag_name in [(args.exclude, "--exclude"), (args.include, "--include")]:
        if not pattern_list:
            continue
        for pattern in pattern_list:
            for known_flag in known_flags:
                if f" {known_flag} " in pattern or (f" {known_flag}" in pattern and pattern.endswith(known_flag)):
                    emit(
                        "ERROR_QUOTING",
                        flag=flag_name,
                        pattern=pattern[:120],
                        embedded=known_flag,
                    )
                    sys.exit(1)
The validation iterates over all registered option strings in the parser, constructing a lookup set without needing hardcoded flag names. It examines each pattern in args.exclude and args.include, checking for boundary-delimited substrings matching " {known_flag} " or trailing patterns ending with " {known_flag}". If an embedded flag is identified, it emits the localized ERROR_QUOTING template—truncating patterns to 120 characters to preserve terminal formatting—and calls sys.exit(1).

Parameters: * parser (argparse.ArgumentParser): The argument parser instance containing registered actions. * args (argparse.Namespace): The parsed arguments containing exclude and include lists.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * SystemExit: Exits with status code 1 if an embedded flag is detected inside any pattern string.

Example: 

# Invocation inside main() prior to executing any pipeline operations:
_check_quoting_errors(parser, args)

docs.title: _run_cleanup()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _run_cleanup() -> None:

Description: Cleans up disk state by removing persistent LLM cache files and clearing session log directories. It deletes the root llm_cache.json file if present, and removes the log directory specified by the LOG_DIR environment variable (defaulting to "logs"). Deletion attempts are wrapped in exception handlers, emitting status telemetry on success and capturing errors via CLEANUP_FAILED without terminating execution.

def _run_cleanup():
    """Clean up cache files and log directory."""
    emit("CLEANUP_START")

    for cache_path in ["llm_cache.json"]:
        if os.path.exists(cache_path):
            try:
                os.remove(cache_path)
                emit("CLEANUP_REMOVED", path=cache_path)
            except Exception as e:
                emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", path=cache_path, error=e)

    log_dir = os.environ.get("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    if os.path.exists(log_dir) and os.path.isdir(log_dir):
        try:
            shutil.rmtree(log_dir)
            emit("CLEANUP_REMOVED_DIR", path=log_dir)
        except Exception as e:
            emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", path=log_dir, error=e)
The cleanup routine uses os.remove for files and shutil.rmtree for directory trees. Status updates are routed through the localized emit logger, tracking progress via CLEANUP_START, CLEANUP_REMOVED, and CLEANUP_REMOVED_DIR. Any encountered file system or OS errors are caught and logged under CLEANUP_FAILED, preventing I/O issues from breaking pipeline runs.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * None. All internal I/O and file system exceptions are caught and reported via emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", ...).

Example: 

# Standalone execution or post-pipeline cleanup:
if args.cleanup:
    _run_cleanup()

docs.text:
The SharedStoreContext is the central dictionary created by build_shared_store() and passed through PocketFlow execution nodes. It holds the complete set of CLI arguments, operational constraints, resolved patterns, and pre-allocated output containers for downstream nodes to populate.

Field Type Description repo_url str \| None Target GitHub repository URL, or None if analyzing local files. local_dir str \| None Target local filesystem directory path, or None if analyzing a repository. project_name str \| None Name of the project, or None if deferred to FetchRepo resolution. github_token str \| None Resolved personal access token for GitHub API interactions. output_dir str Base root directory for pipeline output generation (defaults to "output"). include_patterns set[str] Set of glob patterns qualifying files for ingestion (defaults to {"*"}). exclude_patterns set[str] Global exclusion set merging DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS with user patterns. max_file_size int Maximum size threshold in bytes for ingested source files (defaults to 200000). language str Target language for generated documentation (defaults to "english"). use_cache bool Flag controlling whether LLM response caching is enabled (not args.no_cache). max_abstraction_num int Upper limit of abstractions to discover (defaults to 10). thinking_level str \| None Reasoning effort constraint passed to supporting LLMs (low, medium, high, or None). max_tokens int \| None Manual token ceiling override for model context limits, or None. mode str Documentation style: "tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", or "sdk". mkdocs bool Whether to generate MkDocs Material configurations, navigation, docs.title: Shell Quoting Corruption Check
docs.text:
Because command shells merge adjacent parameters when quotes are misplaced (for example, --exclude "src/* "test/*" --language ja), subsequent flags can be inadvertently swallowed into string values. main.py detects this via _check_quoting_errors() by scanning input patterns for embedded CLI flags registered in parser._actions. If detected, it emits ERROR_QUOTING with diagnostic context and terminates execution immediately:

for pattern in pattern_list:
    for known_flag in known_flags:
        if f" {known_flag} " in pattern or (f" {known_flag}" in pattern and pattern.endswith(known_flag)):
            emit(
                "ERROR_QUOTING",
                flag=flag_name,
                pattern=pattern[:120],
                embedded=known_flag,
            )
            sys.exit(1)

docs.title: Mutually Exclusive and Required Input Verification
docs.text:
The command-line parser enforces input target requirements through a mutually exclusive group for --repo and --dir. In addition, main() checks that either a repository, directory, or the --cleanup flag is present, halting execution with an argparse.ArgumentError if no target is specified:

if not args.dir and not args.repo:
    parser.error("one of the arguments --repo --dir --cleanup is required")

docs.title: Mode and Cache Invariant Enforcement
docs.text: The module validates documentation generation modes against unsupported flag combinations, preventing execution halts deeper in the pipeline: 1. Incremental Cache Mode Enforcement: Incremental processing is restricted to api-reference mode. If --incremental is passed with other modes, the module emits WARN_INCREMENTAL_API_ONLY and disables the flag. 2. Forced Rebuild Validation: Setting --force-rebuild without --incremental triggers ERROR_FORCE_REBUILD_NO_INCREMENTAL, terminating the process with sys.exit(1). 3. Batching Mode Conflicts: If --force-batch is supplied in api-reference mode, the module emits WARN_FORCE_BATCH_API_REF and resets the flag to False, as API reference mode uses deterministic mapping rather than map-reduce batching.

docs.title: GitHub Credential Fallbacks
docs.text:
When generating documentation for remote repositories without authentication, the module emits a warning rather than failing immediately, allowing public repositories to be fetched within default unauthenticated rate limits:

if args.repo:
    github_token = args.token or os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN")
    if not github_token:
        emit("WARN_NO_GITHUB_TOKEN")
elif args.token:
    emit("WARN_TOKEN_NO_REPO")

docs.title: Non-Fatal Maintenance Operations
docs.text:
The _run_cleanup() routine wraps all disk operations in broad exception handlers. If file permission issues or missing paths occur while deleting llm_cache.json or removing the directory specified by LOG_DIR, the error is intercepted and reported via CLEANUP_FAILED, allowing the pipeline to proceed without crashing:

try:
    shutil.rmtree(log_dir)
    emit("CLEANUP_REMOVED_DIR", path=log_dir)
except Exception as e:
    emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", path=log_dir, error=e)

docs.title: Teardown and Resource Cleanup Guarantee
docs.text:
To prevent dangling file descriptors, unbuffered log losses, or hanging network streams, pipeline execution is wrapped in a try...finally block that invokes shutdown() from utils/output.py during process termination:

try:
    tutorial_flow.run(shared)
    if args.cleanup:
        _run_cleanup()
finally:
    from utils.output import shutdown

    shutdown()

docs.title: nodes.py
docs.text: Source: nodes.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The execution sequence orchestrated by main.py initializes global configuration, resolves runtime credentials, and populates the shared blackboard store before passing execution control to flow.py. In turn, flow.py defines the directed acyclic graph (DAG) topology using the PocketFlow engine. nodes.py serves as the concrete operational engine of this architecture, implementing every computational step, filesystem crawler adapter, Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning prompt, and site synthesizer.

The module provides ten discrete node implementations extending PocketFlow's Node and BatchNode base classes. These nodes span local and remote repository ingestion (FetchRepo), volumetric context estimation and dynamic execution path branching (ContextRouter), deterministic file filtering (DeterministicFileMapper), single-pass and batched conceptual abstraction extraction (IdentifyAbstractions, MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions), architectural relationship mapping (AnalyzeRelationships), topological chapter sequencing (OrderChapters), stateful incremental chapter drafting (WriteChapters), and static documentation compilation (CombineTutorial).

Node operations adhere to a strict three-phase lifecycle: prep() extracts and formats data from the blackboard context, exec() performs computation or LLM inference, and post() mutates the shared state or directs DAG routing. All LLM-facing exec() methods are wrapped with the @safe_exec decorator to standardize exception logging and retry tracking. State transfer between nodes is mediated through a mutable shared dictionary, decoupling node implementations while maintaining transactional data consistency.

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class DeterministicFileMapper(Node):

Description: A specialized pipeline node that bypasses conceptual abstraction clustering for API reference documentation generation. It prompts the LLM to inspect the complete indexed codebase file listing, filter out non-code assets (e.g., configurations, test fixtures, static text), and directly maps each remaining source file into an isolated documentation module ordered hierarchically by directory depth.

class DeterministicFileMapper(Node):
    def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        project_name = shared["project_name"]

        file_listing = "\n".join([f"{i} # {path}" for i, (path, _) in enumerate(files_data)])

        prompt = build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name, file_listing)
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"DeterministicFileMapper prep | {len(files_data)} candidate files for filtering", dest="LOG")
        return prompt, shared.get("use_cache", True), shared.get("thinking_level", None), shared.get("max_tokens", 100000)

The class inherits from Node and structures execution into filtering preparation, LLM inference, and deterministic chapter assignment. By mapping individual source code files directly to chapters, it establishes a predictable one-to-one documentation layout suitable for formal API documentation suites.

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Extracts the repository file list from the shared context, formats an indexed coordinate manifest ({i} # {path}), and invokes build_code_file_filter_prompt() to construct the LLM prompt.

Parameters: * shared (dict): The global workflow dictionary containing ingested files, project_name, and execution flags.

Returns: * tuple: A 4-element tuple consisting of (prompt, use_cache, thinking_level, max_tokens).

Example: 

# Extracted from DeterministicFileMapper.prep implementation
files_data = shared["files"]
project_name = shared["project_name"]

file_listing = "\n".join([f"{i} # {path}" for i, (path, _) in enumerate(files_data)])

prompt = build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name, file_listing)
emit_raw("DEBUG", f"DeterministicFileMapper prep | {len(files_data)} candidate files for filtering", dest="LOG")

The method formats file indices and paths into a compact string representation to minimize prompt token overhead. It delegates prompt assembly to utils.prompts.build_code_file_filter_prompt and reads caching and reasoning parameters defensively from the shared store.

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> list[int]:

Description: Dispatches the filtering prompt to the LLM via call_llm(), parses the returned YAML block into a list of valid integer file indices, and strips invalid non-list responses.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): The tuple (prompt, use_cache, thinking_level, max_tokens) generated by prep().

Returns: * list[int]: A list of validated integer indices representing source code files to document.

Raises: * Exception: Any network or model inference exception intercepted and re-raised by @safe_exec.

Example: 

# Extracted from DeterministicFileMapper.exec implementation
@safe_exec
def exec(self, prep_res):
    prompt, use_cache, thinking_level, max_tokens = prep_res
    emit("LLM_CALL_FILTER_FILES")
    log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, max_tokens)
    response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level)
    valid_indices = parse_yaml_response(response)
    if not isinstance(valid_indices, list):
        valid_indices = []
    return [int(idx) for idx in valid_indices]

The method incorporates retry tracking, bypassing cache lookups (cur_retry == 0) on repeated attempts following execution failures. Responses are deserialized using parse_yaml_response() and converted strictly to integer values to prevent downstream indexing errors.

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: tuple, exec_res: list[int]) -> str:

Description: Converts validated file indices into module descriptors, orders modules by directory depth, and populates the shared store.

docs.title: Phase 1: Module Extraction and Filtering
docs.text:
files = shared.get("files", [])
valid_indices = set(exec_res)
modules = []
chapter_order = []

for idx, (file_path, _content) in enumerate(files):
    if idx not in valid_indices:
        emit("SKIP_NON_CODE_FILE", path=file_path)
        continue

    clean_name = os.path.basename(file_path)

    modules.append(
        {"name": clean_name, "description": f"Internal API reference for `{file_path}`", "files": [idx], "original_path": file_path}
    )
    chapter_order.append(len(modules) - 1)

The first phase iterates through all crawled files, cross-referencing each file index against valid_indices. Files omitted by the LLM filter trigger SKIP_NON_CODE_FILE events. Retained files are converted into abstraction module dicts containing the file base name, descriptive reference label, single-element index array, and the relative repository path.

docs.title: Phase 2: Depth-Based Chapter Ordering and State Persistence
docs.text:
shared["abstractions"] = modules
# Sort chapter order by directory depth (deepest first, then alphabetical).
# This ensures utility/leaf files are processed before orchestration files,
# so their summaries are available as cross-chapter context.
# Works universally across all languages (Python, C#, C++, Java, etc.).
shared["chapter_order"] = sorted(
    chapter_order,
    key=lambda idx: (
        -modules[idx]["original_path"].count("/") - modules[idx]["original_path"].count(os.sep),
        modules[idx]["original_path"].lower(),
    ),
)
shared["relationships"] = {"summary": "Deterministic Internal API Reference.", "details": []}
emit("DONE_DETERMINISTIC_MAPPER", count=len(modules))
return "default"

The second phase calculates path separator frequencies (/ and os.sep) to sort chapters in descending order of directory depth. Deeply nested leaf utilities are scheduled for documentation before higher-level orchestrators, ensuring that leaf module summaries are available as cross-chapter context during downstream chapter drafting. The method stores abstractions, chapter_order, and a static relationships payload into shared, returning "default" to advance the workflow DAG.

docs.title: ContextRouter
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class ContextRouter(Node):

Description: The volumetric profiling and flow dispatch controller of the pipeline. It calculates LLM prompt template overhead, measures codebase token volumes, compares them against dynamic model capacity ceilings, and routes execution down one of three paths: "deterministic", "direct", or "batch".

class ContextRouter(Node):
    # Lifecycle methods: prep(), exec(), post()
    pass

The router serves as the central traffic switch in the architecture. When projects exceed prompt capacity limits, ContextRouter creates token-bounded, directory-coherent file chunks, preventing context window overflow during downstream abstraction discovery.

docs.title: ContextRouter.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Conducts static token profiling across prompt templates, directory trees, chapter listings, and source code files to establish the effective token budget and determine the routing strategy.

docs.title: Phase 1: Context Overhead Estimation
docs.text:
files_data = shared["files"]
max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)

shared["max_tokens"] = max_tokens

# --- Calculate prompt overhead FIRST ---
# 1. Prompt templates: check both IA/MA (for batching) and WC (for chapter writing)
#    Use the largest template across all modes as worst-case estimate
prompt_dir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "prompts")
max_template_tokens = 0
for subdir in ["tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", "sdk"]:
    for template_name in ["map_abstractions.md", "identify_abstractions.md", "draft_chapters.md"]:
        template_path = os.path.join(prompt_dir, subdir, template_name)
        if os.path.exists(template_path):
            with open(template_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                t = count_tokens(f.read())
            max_template_tokens = max(max_template_tokens, t)

# 2. Directory tree (shared across IA, MA, and WC prompts)
directory_tree = build_directory_tree(files_data)
tree_tokens = count_tokens(directory_tree)

# 3. Chapter listing estimate (used in WC draft_chapters prompts)
chapter_listing_estimate = "\n".join(f"{i + 1}. {os.path.basename(path)} (doc: {path}.md)" for i, (path, _) in enumerate(files_data))
listing_tokens = count_tokens(chapter_listing_estimate)

prompt_overhead = max_template_tokens + tree_tokens + listing_tokens
emit(
    "CAPACITY_PROMPT_OVERHEAD",
    total=f"{prompt_overhead:,}",
    template=f"{max_template_tokens:,}",
    tree=f"{tree_tokens:,}",
    listing=f"{listing_tokens:,}",
)

The first phase estimates worst-case prompt overhead before inspecting file contents. It loads template files across modes (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk), tokenizes the directory tree built via build_directory_tree(), and estimates chapter index formatting costs. Summing these metrics produces prompt_overhead, reserving necessary context capacity for system instructions and metadata.

docs.title: Phase 2: Content Token Auditing and Safety Limit Computation
docs.text:
total_tokens = 0
file_token_map = []
for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
    entry = f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"
    tokens = count_tokens(entry)
    total_tokens += tokens
    file_token_map.append(tokens)

# --- Effective limit = safety margin minus overhead ---
safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)
effective_limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead
force_batch = shared.get("force_batch", False)

The second phase iterates through all crawled source files, formatting each into an indexed block to calculate precise BPE token metrics using count_tokens(). It maintains a file_token_map array for file-level lookups and sets an operational ceiling of 95% of max_tokens. Subtracting prompt_overhead from this safety limit yields the effective_limit for source code ingestion.

docs.title: Phase 3: Route Decision Evaluation
docs.text:
if shared.get("mode", "tutorial") == "api-reference":
    emit("CAPACITY_API_REF_MODE")
    return ("deterministic", files_data, effective_limit, shared.get("batch_size", 50), None, None, directory_tree)

if total_tokens > effective_limit and force_batch:
    emit("CAPACITY_EXCEEDS_FORCE", tokens=f"{total_tokens:,}", limit=f"{effective_limit:,}", safety=f"{safety_limit:,}", overhead=f"{prompt_overhead:,}")
elif total_tokens > effective_limit:
    emit("CAPACITY_EXCEEDS", tokens=f"{total_tokens:,}", limit=f"{effective_limit:,}", safety=f"{safety_limit:,}", overhead=f"{prompt_overhead:,}")
elif force_batch:
    emit("CAPACITY_FITS_FORCE", tokens=f"{total_tokens:,}", limit=f"{effective_limit:,}", safety=f"{safety_limit:,}", overhead=f"{prompt_overhead:,}")
else:
    emit("CAPACITY_FITS", tokens=f"{total_tokens:,}", limit=f"{effective_limit:,}", safety=f"{safety_limit:,}", overhead=f"{prompt_overhead:,}")
    return ("direct", files_data, effective_limit, shared.get("batch_size", 50), None, None, directory_tree)

return (
    "batch",
    files_data,
    effective_limit,
    shared.get("batch_size", 50),
    file_token_map,
    count_tokens,
    directory_tree,
)

The final phase evaluates execution parameters to select the routing mode. The "api-reference" mode immediately selects "deterministic". Otherwise, if total_tokens fits within effective_limit without force_batch enabled, it selects the "direct" route. If total content exceeds capacity or batching is explicitly forced, it returns "batch" alongside file_token_map.

docs.title: ContextRouter.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> str | list[list[tuple]]:

Description: Executes routing logic, packaging files into token-bounded, directory-coherent batches when the "batch" route is active.

docs.title: Phase 1: Pass-Through Routing Check
docs.text:
route, files_data, effective_limit, batch_size, file_token_map, _count_tokens, directory_tree = prep_res
emit_raw(
    "DEBUG",
    f"NODE EXEC | node=ContextRouter | action=route_decision | route={route} | files={len(files_data)} | effective_limit={effective_limit:,}",
    dest="LOG",
)

if route == "direct":
    return "direct"
if route == "deterministic":
    return "deterministic"

For "direct" and "deterministic" routing configurations, exec() acts as a pass-through return mechanism. It emits diagnostic state to the log sink and immediately returns the selected route string without performing file grouping operations.

docs.title: Phase 2: Directory-Aware Batch Clustering
docs.text:
# Group by directory for coherence, with pre-computed tokens
dir_groups = defaultdict(list)
for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
    dir_groups[os.path.dirname(path)].append((i, path, content, file_token_map[i]))

# Build token-aware batches (never mix directories)
batches = []
for dirname in sorted(dir_groups.keys()):
    current_batch = []
    current_tokens = 0

    for i, path, content, tokens in dir_groups[dirname]:
        # Start new batch if adding this file would exceed effective limit or file count cap
        if current_batch and (current_tokens + tokens > effective_limit or len(current_batch) >= batch_size):
            batches.append(current_batch)
            current_batch = []
            current_tokens = 0

        current_batch.append((i, path, content))
        current_tokens += tokens

    # Flush remaining files in this directory
    if current_batch:
        batches.append(current_batch)

batch_word = "batch" if len(batches) == 1 else "batches"
emit("CAPACITY_SPLIT", count=len(batches), word=batch_word)
self._directory_tree = directory_tree
return batches

When batching is required, files are grouped by parent directory (os.path.dirname) to preserve architectural coherence. Batches are accumulated sequentially per directory without mixing files across separate directories. A new batch is initiated whenever adding a file would exceed effective_limit or the batch_size limit (default 50). The pre-computed directory_tree is saved to self._directory_tree, and the list of batch lists is returned.

docs.title: ContextRouter.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: tuple, exec_res: str | list) -> str:

Description: Persists routing artifacts to the shared store and returns the action edge string that drives conditional DAG branching in flow.py.

def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"ContextRouter post | route={'batch' if isinstance(exec_res, list) else exec_res}", dest="LOG")
    if exec_res == "direct":
        return "direct"
    if exec_res == "deterministic":
        return "deterministic"
    shared["file_batches"] = exec_res
    # Reuse directory tree built during prep()
    shared["directory_tree"] = getattr(self, "_directory_tree", build_directory_tree(shared["files"]))
    return "batch"

The method inspects exec_res to branch execution. For scalar strings ("direct" or "deterministic"), it returns them as the active action label. For list payloads, it assigns exec_res to shared["file_batches"], caches directory_tree in shared, and returns "batch".

docs.title: MapAbstractions
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class MapAbstractions(BatchNode):

Description: A parallelized BatchNode that processes directory-bounded file batches generated by ContextRouter. It prompts the LLM to analyze the files in each batch against the project directory tree and identify local conceptual abstractions.

class MapAbstractions(BatchNode):

Inheriting from BatchNode, this class processes work items generated by prep() through exec(). Each batch produces partial abstraction records that are subsequently aggregated in post() and resolved by ReduceAbstractions.

docs.title: MapAbstractions.prep()
docs.text:

Description: Transforms shared["file_batches"] into a list of isolated work-item dictionaries for batch execution.

Parameters: * shared (dict): The global workflow dictionary containing file_batches, project_name, language, and execution settings.

Returns: * list[dict]: An iterable list of dictionary configurations passed to exec().

Example: 

# Extracted from MapAbstractions.prep implementation
return [
    {
        "batch_index": i,
        "files": batch,
        "project_name": shared["project_name"],
        "language": shared.get("language", "english"),

    for i, batch in enumerate(shared["file_batches"])

The method formats work items with execution parameters including batch indices, file entries, localization targets, caching flags, context limits, and the directory tree.

docs.title: MapAbstractions.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, item: dict) -> list[dict]:

Description: Executes abstraction discovery over a single file batch, formatting the prompt, tracking token consumption, and validating the parsed abstraction objects.

docs.title: Phase 1: Prompt Construction and Token Tracking
docs.text:
batch_index = item["batch_index"]
files = item["files"]
emit("LLM_CALL_MAP_ABSTRACTIONS", batch_index=batch_index, file_count=len(files))

context = ""
for i, path, content in files:
    context += f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"

prompt_template = load_prompt_template("map_abstractions", mode=item.get("mode", "tutorial"))

language = item.get("language", "english")
language_instruction = f"Output language MUST be entirely in {language.capitalize()}. " if language.lower() != "english" else ""
name_lang_hint = f" (in {language.capitalize()})" if language.lower() != "english" else ""
desc_lang_hint = f" (in {language.capitalize()})" if language.lower() != "english" else ""

prompt = prompt_template.format(
    project_name=item["project_name"],
    context=context,
    language_instruction=language_instruction,
    name_lang_hint=name_lang_hint,
    desc_lang_hint=desc_lang_hint,
    directory_tree=item.get("directory_tree", "Not available"),
)

token_usage = {
    "file_content": count_tokens(context),
    "directory_tree": count_tokens(item.get("directory_tree", "")),
}
token_usage["overhead"] = count_tokens(prompt) - sum(token_usage.values())
log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, item["max_tokens"], token_usage=token_usage)

The first phase serializes the batch's files into an indexed context block and retrieves the map_abstractions prompt template. It injects language directives when language is not English, interpolates prompt variables, computes component token metrics (file_content, directory_tree, overhead), and logs token capacity telemetry via log_token_estimation().

docs.title: Phase 2: Inference and Schema Sanitization
docs.text:
for i, path, _content in files:
    emit("BATCH_FILE_ITEM", index=i, path=path)
response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(item["use_cache"] and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=item["thinking_level"])

abstractions = parse_yaml_response(response)

validated_abstractions = []
if isinstance(abstractions, list):
    for obj in abstractions:
        if isinstance(obj, dict) and "name" in obj and "description" in obj and "file_indices" in obj:
            validated_indices = []
            for idx_entry in obj["file_indices"]:
                idx = parse_file_index(idx_entry)
                if idx is not None:
                    validated_indices.append(idx)
            if validated_indices:
                validated_abstractions.append(
                    {"name": obj["name"], "description": obj["description"], "files": sorted(set(validated_indices))}
                )
return validated_abstractions

The second phase emits per-file progress events, dispatches the prompt through call_llm(), and parses the YAML response via parse_yaml_response(). It iterates through candidate abstraction objects, verifying required keys (name, description, file_indices) and resolving file index entries through parse_file_index(). Deduplicated, sorted index arrays are preserved in the returned abstraction records.

docs.title: MapAbstractions.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: list[dict], exec_res_list: list[list[dict]]) -> None:

Description: Flattens abstraction records from all completed batch executions and stores the aggregated list in shared["mapped_abstractions"].

def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res_list):
    all_abstractions = []
    for batch_abs in exec_res_list:
        all_abstractions.extend(batch_abs)
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"MapAbstractions post | collected {len(all_abstractions)} partial abstractions", dest="LOG")
    shared["mapped_abstractions"] = all_abstractions

The method aggregates nested abstraction lists from exec_res_list into a single flat array. It logs the total count of discovered abstractions and stores them in shared["mapped_abstractions"] for consolidation by ReduceAbstractions.

docs.title: ReduceAbstractions
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class ReduceAbstractions(Node):

Description: The reduction companion to MapAbstractions. It consolidates, deduplicates, and refines the set of partial abstractions discovered across batches into a cohesive, high-level architectural abstraction catalog.

class ReduceAbstractions(Node):
    # Lifecycle methods: prep(), exec(), post()
    pass

The node limits conceptual sprawl by synthesizing partial abstractions into an interconnected set bounded by max_abstraction_num.

docs.title: ReduceAbstractions.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Extracts mapped_abstractions and related configuration settings from shared into a parameter tuple for execution.

def prep(self, shared):

        shared["mapped_abstractions"],

The method packages the reduction context, including abstraction records, project identity, localization parameters, and abstraction ceilings (defaulting to 10).

docs.title: ReduceAbstractions.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> list[dict]:

Description: Formats the partial abstractions into a consolidation prompt, invokes the model, and validates the unified abstraction catalog.

docs.title: Phase 1: Abstraction Consolidation Prompt Assembly
docs.text:
mapped_abstractions, project_name, language, use_cache, max_abstraction_num, thinking_level, _advanced_mode, max_tokens, mode = prep_res

context = ""
for i, abs_obj in enumerate(mapped_abstractions):
    context += f"- Partial Abstraction {i}: {abs_obj['name']}\n  Description: {abs_obj['description']}\n  Files: {abs_obj['files']}\n\n"

prompt_template = load_prompt_template("reduce_abstractions", mode=mode)

language_instruction = f"Output language MUST be entirely in {language.capitalize()}. " if language.lower() != "english" else ""
name_lang_hint = f" (in {language.capitalize()})" if language.lower() != "english" else ""
desc_lang_hint = f" (in {language.capitalize()})" if language.lower() != "english" else ""

prompt = prompt_template.format(
    project_name=project_name,
    partial_abstractions=context,
    max_abstraction_num=max_abstraction_num,
    language_instruction=language_instruction,
    name_lang_hint=name_lang_hint,
    desc_lang_hint=desc_lang_hint,
)

The first phase serializes partial abstractions into a formatted Markdown list showing the name, description, and constituent file indices for each item. It injects localization directives when operating in non-English modes, bounds the output via max_abstraction_num, and interpolates the template loaded via load_prompt_template("reduce_abstractions").

docs.title: Phase 2: Inference and Abstraction Index Validation
docs.text:
emit("LLM_CALL_REDUCE_ABSTRACTIONS", count=len(mapped_abstractions))
log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, max_tokens)
response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level)

abstractions = parse_yaml_response(response)

validated_abstractions = []
if isinstance(abstractions, list):
    for obj in abstractions:
        if isinstance(obj, dict) and "name" in obj and "description" in obj and "files" in obj:
            validated_indices = []
            for idx_entry in obj["files"]:
                idx = parse_file_index(idx_entry)
                if idx is not None:
                    validated_indices.append(idx)
            if validated_indices:
                validated_abstractions.append(
                    {"name": obj["name"], "description": obj["description"], "files": sorted(set(validated_indices))}
                )
return validated_abstractions

The second phase emits progress indicators, evaluates token consumption against context limits, and dispatches the consolidation request to call_llm(). Deserialized YAML responses are validated to ensure each entry contains name, description, and files keys. Constituent indices are resolved via parse_file_index(), deduplicated, sorted, and returned as the final abstraction catalog.

docs.title: FetchRepo
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class FetchRepo(Node):

Description: The entry point ingestion node of the pipeline. It resolves target repository references (local directory path or remote Git URL), applies file filtering and size constraints, and converts codebase contents into an indexed in-memory representation.

class FetchRepo(Node):
    # Lifecycle methods: prep(), exec(), post()
    pass

The node acts as a facade over crawl_github_files and crawl_local_files, providing downstream consumers with a unified list[tuple[str, str]] file representation.

docs.title: FetchRepo.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> dict:

Description: Resolves the project name from repository metadata and extracts filtering parameters from the shared store.

def prep(self, shared):
    repo_url = shared.get("repo_url")
    local_dir = shared.get("local_dir")
    project_name = shared.get("project_name")

    if not project_name:
        # Basic name derivation from URL or directory
        if repo_url:
            project_name = repo_url.split("/")[-1].replace(".git", "")
        else:
            project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(local_dir))
        shared["project_name"] = project_name

    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG", f"FetchRepo prep | project_name='{project_name}' | source='{shared.get('repo_url') or shared.get('local_dir', '.')}'", dest="LOG"
    )

    # Get file patterns directly from shared
    include_patterns = shared["include_patterns"]
    exclude_patterns = shared["exclude_patterns"]
    max_file_size = shared["max_file_size"]

    return {
        "repo_url": repo_url,
        "local_dir": local_dir,
        "token": shared.get("github_token"),
        "include_patterns": include_patterns,
        "exclude_patterns": exclude_patterns,
        "max_file_size": max_file_size,
        "use_relative_paths": True,
    }

The method derives project_name from the target URL or directory path when not explicitly provided. It bundles file matching globs, exclusion expressions, authentication tokens, and size bounds into the execution dictionary.

docs.title: FetchRepo.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: dict) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:

Description: Executes repository crawling using the appropriate local or remote crawler and normalizes the results into an ordered list of (relative_path, content) tuples.

def exec(self, prep_res):
    source = prep_res["repo_url"] or prep_res["local_dir"]
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"NODE EXEC | node=FetchRepo | action=crawl_files | source={source}", dest="LOG")

    if prep_res["repo_url"]:
        emit("CRAWL_REPOSITORY", url=prep_res["repo_url"])
        result = crawl_github_files(
            repo_url=prep_res["repo_url"],
            token=prep_res["token"],
            include_patterns=prep_res["include_patterns"],
            exclude_patterns=prep_res["exclude_patterns"],
            max_file_size=prep_res["max_file_size"],
            use_relative_paths=prep_res["use_relative_paths"],
        )
    else:
        emit("CRAWL_DIRECTORY", path=prep_res["local_dir"])

        result = crawl_local_files(
            directory=prep_res["local_dir"],
            include_patterns=prep_res["include_patterns"],
            exclude_patterns=prep_res["exclude_patterns"],
            max_file_size=prep_res["max_file_size"],
            use_relative_paths=prep_res["use_relative_paths"],
        )

    # Convert dict to list of tuples: [(path, content), ...]
    files_list = list(result.get("files", {}).items())
    if len(files_list) == 0:
        raise ValueError("No matching files found. Check your directory and include/exclude patterns.")

    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"NODE COMPLETE | node=FetchRepo | files_found={len(files_list)}", dest="LOG")
    return files_list

The method routes crawling based on whether repo_url is present, invoking crawl_github_files() for remote repositories or crawl_local_files() for local directories. The returned mapping is converted to a list of (path, content) tuples. If no qualifying files match the inclusion filters, it raises a ValueError.

docs.title: IdentifyAbstractions
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class IdentifyAbstractions(Node):

Description: Performs single-pass conceptual abstraction discovery for codebases that fit within the effective context window limit. It formats all qualifying source files into a single prompt, instructing the LLM to extract primary components, subsystem responsibilities, and constituent file coordinate indices.

class IdentifyAbstractions(Node):
    # Lifecycle methods: prep(), exec(), post()
    pass

The class uses @safe_exec to wrap its exec() method, providing automated error logging and retry handling during LLM inference and schema validation.

docs.title: IdentifyAbstractions.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Formats source file contents within token capacity bounds, generates the repository directory tree, and packages execution parameters.

def prep(self, shared):
    files_data = shared["files"]
    project_name = shared["project_name"]  # Get project name
    language = shared.get("language", "english")  # Get language
    use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)  # Get use_cache flag, default to True
    max_abstraction_num = shared.get("max_abstraction_num", 10)  # Get max_abstraction_num, default to 10
    thinking_level = shared.get("thinking_level", None)

    # Helper to create context from files, respecting limits (basic example)
    def create_llm_context(files_data):
        # Retrieve max tokens limit
        max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)

        safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)

        context = ""
        current_tokens = 0

        for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
            entry = f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"

            entry_tokens = count_tokens(entry)

            if current_tokens + entry_tokens > safety_limit:
                emit("WARN_CONTEXT_TRUNCATED", index=i, path=path, limit=safety_limit)
                break

            context += entry
            current_tokens += entry_tokens

        return context

    context = create_llm_context(files_data)
    directory_tree = build_directory_tree(files_data)
    current_tokens = count_tokens(context)
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"IdentifyAbstractions prep | context_tokens={current_tokens:,} | files={len(files_data)}", dest="LOG")
    return (
        context,
        directory_tree,
        len(files_data),
        project_name,
        language,
        use_cache,
        max_abstraction_num,
        thinking_level,
        shared.get("advanced_mode", False),
        shared.get("max_tokens", 100000),
        shared.get("mode", "tutorial"),
    )  # Return all parameters (11-element tuple)

The method uses the nested helper create_llm_context to append files sequentially until the 95% safety ceiling is reached. It generates a directory tree representation via build_directory_tree(), measures context tokens, and returns an 11-element parameter tuple.

docs.title: IdentifyAbstractions.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> list[dict]:

Description: Dispatches the single-pass abstraction prompt, parses the YAML completion, validates schema types, and resolves file index references.

docs.title: Phase 1: Prompt Templating and Token Estimation
docs.text:
(
    context,
    directory_tree,
    total_files_count,
    project_name,
    language,
    use_cache,
    max_abstraction_num,
    thinking_level,
    _advanced_mode,
    max_tokens,
    mode,
) = prep_res  # Unpack all parameters

# Add language instruction and hints only if not English
language_instruction = ""
name_lang_hint = ""
desc_lang_hint = ""
if language.lower() != "english":
    language_instruction = f"IMPORTANT: Generate the `name` and `description` for each abstraction in **{language.capitalize()}** language. Do NOT use English for these fields.\n\n"
    # Keep specific hints here as name/description are primary targets
    name_lang_hint = f" (value in {language.capitalize()})"
    desc_lang_hint = f" (value in {language.capitalize()})"

prompt_template = load_prompt_template("identify_abstractions", mode=mode)

prompt = prompt_template.format(
    project_name=project_name,
    context=context,
    language_instruction=language_instruction,
    max_abstraction_num=max_abstraction_num,
    name_lang_hint=name_lang_hint,
    desc_lang_hint=desc_lang_hint,
    directory_tree=directory_tree,
)

token_usage = {
    "file_content": count_tokens(context),
    "directory_tree": count_tokens(directory_tree),
}
token_usage["overhead"] = count_tokens(prompt) - sum(token_usage.values())
emit("LLM_CALL_IDENTIFY_ABSTRACTIONS")
log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, max_tokens, token_usage=token_usage)

The first phase unpacks configuration values, formats language-specific instructions, loads the prompt template, and interpolates context variables. It breaks down token consumption into file content, directory tree, and overhead, logging the estimates before invoking call_llm().

docs.title: Phase 2: Parsing and Index Range Resolution
docs.text:
abstractions = parse_yaml_response(response)

if not isinstance(abstractions, list):
    raise ValueError("LLM Output is not a list")

validated_abstractions = []
for item in abstractions:
    if not isinstance(item, dict) or not all(k in item for k in ["name", "description", "file_indices"]):
        raise ValueError(f"Missing keys in abstraction item: {item}")
    if not isinstance(item["name"], str):
        raise ValueError(f"Name is not a string in item: {item}")
    if not isinstance(item["description"], str):
        raise ValueError(f"Description is not a string in item: {item}")
    if not isinstance(item["file_indices"], list):
        raise ValueError(f"file_indices is not a list in item: {item}")

    # Validate indices
    validated_indices = []
    for idx_entry in item["file_indices"]:
        try:
            idx_str = str(idx_entry).split("#")[0].strip()
            # Split by '-' to handle ranges
            if "-" in idx_str:
                parts = idx_str.split("-")
                if len(parts) == 2:
                    start_idx = parse_file_index(parts[0])
                    end_idx = parse_file_index(parts[1])
                    if start_idx is not None and end_idx is not None:
                        validated_indices.extend(idx for idx in range(start_idx, end_idx + 1) if 0 <= idx < total_files_count)
                    continue
            # Find integer in the string
            idx = parse_file_index(idx_str)
            if idx is not None and 0 <= idx < total_files_count:
                validated_indices.append(idx)
        except (ValueError, TypeError, IndexError):
            emit("WARN_PARSE_INDEX", entry=idx_entry, name=item["name"])
            continue

    item["files"] = sorted(set(validated_indices))
    validated_abstractions.append(
        {
            "name": item["name"],
            "description": item["description"],
            "files": item["files"],
        }
    )

emit("DONE_IDENTIFIED_ABSTRACTIONS", count=len(validated_abstractions))
return validated_abstractions

The second phase validates the parsed YAML structure, ensuring required keys and data types are present. Index values are resolved by stripping comment annotations (#), expanding hyphenated index ranges (e.g., 0-3), filtering out out-of-bounds indices, and removing duplicates. Validated records are packaged into dictionary objects containing name, description, and files.
