docs.title: AnalyzeRelationships.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Compiles abstraction catalogs and executes a two-pass token redistribution algorithm to include code snippets across all abstractions without overflowing the prompt budget.

docs.title: Phase 1: Abstraction Listing Assembly
docs.text:
abstractions = shared["abstractions"]  # Now contains 'files' list of indices, name/description potentially translated
files_data = shared["files"]
project_name = shared["project_name"]  # Get project name
language = shared.get("language", "english")  # Get language
use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)  # Get use_cache flag, default to True
thinking_level = shared.get("thinking_level", None)

# Get the actual number of abstractions directly
num_abstractions = len(abstractions)

# Create context with abstraction names, indices, descriptions, and relevant file snippets
context = "Identified Abstractions:\n"
all_relevant_indices = set()
abstraction_info_for_prompt = []
for i, abstr in enumerate(abstractions):
    file_indices_str = ", ".join(map(str, abstr["files"]))
    info_line = f"- Index {i}: {abstr['name']} (Relevant file indices: [{file_indices_str}])\n  Description: {abstr['description']}"
    context += info_line + "\n"
    abstraction_info_for_prompt.append(f"{i} # {abstr['name']}")
    all_relevant_indices.update(abstr["files"])

context += "\nRelevant File Snippets (per abstraction, budget-aware):\n"
max_tokens = shared.get("max_tokens", 100000)
safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)
prompt_overhead = 2000

current_tokens = count_tokens(context)
total_budget = safety_limit - current_tokens - prompt_overhead

The first phase serializes abstraction names, indices, descriptions, and referenced files into an initial catalog string. It calculates available snippet capacity by subtracting the current token count and a 2,000-token prompt overhead from the 95% safety ceiling.

docs.title: Phase 2: Two-Pass Proportional Token Allocation
docs.text:
# Pre-compute file token sizes for all abstractions
abstr_file_data = []
for abstr in abstractions:
    sized = []
    for idx in abstr["files"]:
        if 0 <= idx < len(files_data):
            path, file_content = files_data[idx]
            entry = f"\n--- File: {idx} # {path} ---\n{file_content}\n"
            sized.append((idx, path, file_content, count_tokens(entry)))
    sized.sort(key=lambda x: x[3], reverse=True)
    abstr_file_data.append(sized)

# Pass 1: give each abstraction an equal share, track unused
per_abstr_budget = total_budget // max(num_abstractions, 1)
included_indices = set()
abstr_results = []

for _i, sized in enumerate(abstr_file_data):
    budget = per_abstr_budget
    included_files = []
    remaining_files = []
    for idx, path, file_content, tokens in sized:
        if idx in included_indices:
            included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
            continue
        if tokens <= budget:
            included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
            budget -= tokens
            included_indices.add(idx)
        else:
            remaining_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
    abstr_results.append((included_files, remaining_files, budget))

# Pass 2: redistribute unused budget to abstractions with remaining files
total_unused = sum(r[2] for r in abstr_results)
if total_unused > 0:
    for i, (included_files, remaining_files, _unused) in enumerate(abstr_results):
        if not remaining_files or total_unused <= 0:
            continue
        still_remaining = []
        for idx, path, file_content, tokens in remaining_files:
            if idx in included_indices:
                included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                continue
            if tokens <= total_unused:
                included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                total_unused -= tokens
                included_indices.add(idx)
            else:
                still_remaining.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
        abstr_results[i] = (included_files, still_remaining, 0)

The second phase measures token sizes for all referenced files, sorting them by length descending to prioritize architecturally significant files. Pass 1 divides the token budget equally among abstractions (total_budget // num_abstractions). Files already included in prior abstractions are referenced without duplicating their content. Pass 2 aggregates unused tokens across abstractions and reallocates them to abstractions with remaining unallocated files.

docs.title: Phase 3: Final Context String Assembly
docs.text:
for i, abstr in enumerate(abstractions):
    included_files, remaining_files, _ = abstr_results[i]
    if included_files or remaining_files:
        context += f"\n--- Abstraction {i}: {abstr['name']} ---\n"
        for idx, path, file_content, _tokens in included_files:
            if file_content is not None:
                context += f"\n--- File: {idx} # {path} ---\n{file_content}\n"
            else:
                context += f"  (File {idx} # {path} -- already shown above)\n"
        if remaining_files:
            rest_list = ", ".join(f"{idx} # {p}" for idx, p, _c, _t in remaining_files)
            context += f"  Other files (path only, budget exhausted): {rest_list}\n"

emit_raw(
    "DEBUG",
    f"AnalyzeRelationships prep | total_budget={total_budget:,} | per_abstr_budget={per_abstr_budget:,} | abstractions={num_abstractions}",
    dest="LOG",
)
return (
    context,
    "\n".join(abstraction_info_for_prompt),
    num_abstractions,
    project_name,
    language,
    use_cache,
    thinking_level,
    shared.get("advanced_mode", False),
    shared.get("max_tokens", 100000),
    shared.get("mode", "tutorial"),
)

The third phase formats the allocated file contents into the context string. Files that fit within the budget include full source text; files exceeding budget limits are listed by path only. The method returns a 10-element parameter tuple for exec().

Description: Queries the model to discover architectural relationships between abstractions, validating directed edges and generating a project overview summary.

docs.title: Phase 1: Prompt Construction and Model Inference
docs.text:
(
    context,
    abstraction_listing,

    project_name,

language_instruction = ""
lang_hint = ""
list_lang_note = ""
if language.lower() != "english":
    language_instruction = f"IMPORTANT: Generate the `summary` and relationship `label` fields in **{language.capitalize()}** language. Do NOT use English for these fields.\n\n"
    lang_hint = f" (in {language.capitalize()})"
    list_lang_note = f" (Names might be in {language.capitalize()})"

prompt_template = load_prompt_template("identify_relationships", mode=mode)

prompt = prompt_template.format(
    project_name=project_name,

    language_instruction=language_instruction,
    lang_hint=lang_hint,

    "context": count_tokens(context),
    "abstraction_listing": count_tokens(abstraction_listing),

The first phase constructs language instructions, formats the prompt template with abstraction listings and code context, and logs token usage before calling call_llm().

docs.title: Phase 2: Schema Parsing and Relationship Normalization
docs.text:
relationships_data = parse_yaml_response(response)

if not isinstance(relationships_data, dict) or not all(k in relationships_data for k in ["summary", "relationships"]):
    raise ValueError("LLM output is not a dict or missing keys ('summary', 'relationships')")
if not isinstance(relationships_data["summary"], str):
    raise ValueError("summary is not a string")
if not isinstance(relationships_data["relationships"], list):
    raise ValueError("relationships is not a list")

validated_relationships = []
for rel in relationships_data["relationships"]:
    if not isinstance(rel, dict) or not all(k in rel for k in ["from_abstraction", "to_abstraction", "label"]):
        raise ValueError(f"Missing keys (expected from_abstraction, to_abstraction, label) in relationship item: {rel}")
    if not isinstance(rel["label"], str):
        raise ValueError(f"Relationship label is not a string: {rel}")

    try:
        from_idx_str = str(rel["from_abstraction"]).split("#")[0].strip()
        to_idx_str = str(rel["to_abstraction"]).split("#")[0].strip()

        from_nums = re.findall(r"\d+", from_idx_str)
        to_nums = re.findall(r"\d+", to_idx_str)

        if not from_nums or not to_nums:
            raise ValueError("Missing valid integer for from_abstraction or to_abstraction.")

        from_idx = int(from_nums[0])
        to_idx = int(to_nums[0])
        if not (0 <= from_idx < num_abstractions and 0 <= to_idx < num_abstractions):
            emit("WARN_INVALID_RELATIONSHIP", from_idx=from_idx, to_idx=to_idx, max_idx=num_abstractions - 1)
            continue
        validated_relationships.append(
            {
                "from": from_idx,
                "to": to_idx,
                "label": rel["label"],
            }
        )
    except (ValueError, TypeError, IndexError) as e:
        emit("WARN_PARSE_RELATIONSHIP", rel=rel, error=e)
        continue

emit("DONE_RELATIONSHIPS")
return {
    "summary": relationships_data["summary"],
    "details": validated_relationships,
}

The second phase validates the parsed YAML dictionary, verifying that summary is a string and relationships is a list of entries with from_abstraction, to_abstraction, and label keys. Node index references are parsed using regular expressions (\d+) to strip annotations and bounds-checked against num_abstractions. The method returns a dictionary containing summary and details.

Description: Queries the LLM for a pedagogical chapter ordering and validates that the result contains each abstraction index exactly once.

docs.title: Phase 1: Prompt Construction and Execution
docs.text:
(
    abstraction_listing,
    context,
    num_abstractions,

The first phase loads the order_chapters template, interpolates the context, logs token metrics, and executes the inference request via call_llm().

docs.title: Phase 2: Permutation and Completeness Verification
docs.text:
ordered_indices_raw = parse_yaml_response(response)

if not isinstance(ordered_indices_raw, list):
    raise ValueError("LLM output is not a list")

ordered_indices = []
seen_indices = set()
for entry in ordered_indices_raw:
    try:
        if isinstance(entry, int):
            idx = entry
        elif isinstance(entry, str) and "#" in entry:
            idx = int(entry.split("#")[0].strip())
        else:
            idx = int(str(entry).strip())

        if not (0 <= idx < num_abstractions):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid index {idx} in ordered list. Max index is {num_abstractions - 1}.")
        if idx in seen_indices:
            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate index {idx} found in ordered list.")
        ordered_indices.append(idx)
        seen_indices.add(idx)

    except (ValueError, TypeError) as e:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not parse index from ordered list entry: {entry}") from e

# Check if all abstractions are included
if len(ordered_indices) != num_abstractions:
    raise ValueError(
        f"Ordered list length ({len(ordered_indices)}) does not match number of abstractions ({num_abstractions}). Missing indices: {set(range(num_abstractions)) - seen_indices}"
    )

emit("DONE_CHAPTER_ORDER", indices=ordered_indices)
return ordered_indices

The second phase parses the YAML response into a list of indices, validating that each entry is within range (0 <= idx < num_abstractions) and that no duplicates exist. It then checks that the total count of ordered indices matches num_abstractions. If any index is missing or duplicated, it raises a ValueError.

docs.title: WriteChapters.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> list[dict]:

Description: Establishes chapter filenames, formats linking tables, initializes summary accumulators, and builds work-item configurations.

docs.title: Phase 1: Filename Allocation and Link Mapping
docs.text:
chapter_order = shared["chapter_order"]
abstractions = shared["abstractions"]
files_data = shared["files"]
language = shared.get("language", "english")
use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)
thinking_level = shared.get("thinking_level", None)

self.chapters_written_so_far = []
self.chapter_summaries = []

# Create a complete list of all chapters
all_chapters = []
chapter_filenames = {}
for i, abstraction_index in enumerate(chapter_order):
    if 0 <= abstraction_index < len(abstractions):
        chapter_num = i + 1
        chapter_name = abstractions[abstraction_index]["name"].replace("\n", " ").strip()
        is_mkdocs = shared.get("mkdocs", False)
        if is_mkdocs and "original_path" in abstractions[abstraction_index]:
            doc_rel_path = abstractions[abstraction_index]["original_path"] + ".md"
            filename = doc_rel_path.replace(os.sep, "/")
        elif is_mkdocs:
            safe_name = "".join(c if c.isalnum() else "_" for c in chapter_name).lower()
            filename = f"{safe_name}.md"
        else:
            safe_name = "".join(c if c.isalnum() else "_" for c in chapter_name).lower()
            filename = f"{i + 1:02d}_{safe_name}.md"

        all_chapters.append(f"{chapter_num}. {chapter_name} (doc: {filename})")
        chapter_filenames[abstraction_index] = {
            "num": chapter_num,
            "name": chapter_name,
            "filename": filename,
        }

full_chapter_listing = "\n".join(all_chapters)

The first phase initializes state lists (chapters_written_so_far, chapter_summaries) on the node instance. It iterates through chapter_order to determine output filenames based on whether MkDocs output mode is active. For API reference modes, filenames mirror the original file path; otherwise, sanitized alphanumeric filenames are used. It formats a full_chapter_listing containing (doc: {filename}) markers, giving the LLM the relative paths needed for cross-chapter linking.

docs.title: Phase 2: Sequential Batch Item Generation
docs.text:
items_to_process = []
for i, abstraction_index in enumerate(chapter_order):
    if 0 <= abstraction_index < len(abstractions):
        abstraction_details = abstractions[abstraction_index]
        related_file_indices = abstraction_details.get("files", [])
        related_files_content_map = get_content_for_indices(files_data, related_file_indices)

        prev_chapter = None
        if i > 0:
            prev_idx = chapter_order[i - 1]
            prev_chapter = chapter_filenames[prev_idx]

        next_chapter = None
        if i < len(chapter_order) - 1:
            next_idx = chapter_order[i + 1]
            next_chapter = chapter_filenames[next_idx]

        current_filename = chapter_filenames[abstraction_index]["filename"]

        items_to_process.append(
            {
                "chapter_num": i + 1,
                "abstraction_index": abstraction_index,
                "abstraction_details": abstraction_details,
                "related_files_content_map": related_files_content_map,
                "project_name": shared["project_name"],
                "full_chapter_listing": full_chapter_listing,
                "current_doc_path": current_filename,
                "directory_tree": shared.get("directory_tree", ""),
                "chapter_filenames": chapter_filenames,
                "prev_chapter": prev_chapter,
                "next_chapter": next_chapter,
                "language": language,
                "use_cache": use_cache,
                "thinking_level": thinking_level,
                "advanced_mode": shared.get("advanced_mode", False),
                "mode": shared.get("mode", "tutorial"),
                "mkdocs": shared.get("mkdocs", False),
                "incremental": shared.get("incremental", False),
                "output_dir": shared.get("output_dir", "output"),
                "filename": current_filename,
                "max_tokens": shared.get("max_tokens", 100000),
            }
        )
    else:
        emit("WARN_INVALID_ABSTRACTION", index=abstraction_index)

emit("PREPARING_WRITE_CHAPTERS", count=len(items_to_process))
return items_to_process

The second phase maps constituent files to their source content via get_content_for_indices(), extracts previous and next chapter transitions from chapter_filenames, and packages self-contained work item dictionaries for sequential processing in exec().

use_cache = item.get("use_cache", True)
thinking_level = item.get("thinking_level", None)
mode = item.get("mode", "tutorial")
is_mkdocs = item.get("mkdocs", False)
incremental = item.get("incremental", False)
output_dir = item.get("output_dir", "output")
filename = item.get("filename")
max_tokens = item.get("max_tokens", 100000)

file_context_str = "\n\n".join(
    f"--- File: {idx_path.split('# ')[1] if '# ' in idx_path else idx_path} ---\n{content}"
    for idx_path, content in item["related_files_content_map"].items()
)

current_hash = None
if incremental and output_dir:
    hasher = hashlib.md5()
    hasher.update(file_context_str.encode("utf-8"))
    current_hash = hasher.hexdigest()

    manifest_path = os.path.join(output_dir, project_name, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
    if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
        try:
            with open(manifest_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                manifest = json.load(f)
            cached_entry = manifest.get(abstraction_name)
            if isinstance(cached_entry, str):
                cached_hash, cached_summary = cached_entry, None
            elif isinstance(cached_entry, dict):
                cached_hash = cached_entry.get("hash")
                cached_summary = cached_entry.get("summary")
            else:
                cached_hash, cached_summary = None, None

            if cached_hash == current_hash:
                file_path = (
                    os.path.join(output_dir, project_name, "docs", "api", filename)
                    if is_mkdocs
                    else os.path.join(output_dir, project_name, filename)
                )
                if os.path.exists(file_path):
                    emit("CACHE_HIT_SKIP", name=abstraction_name)
                    with open(file_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                        cached_content = f.read()

                    clean_content = cached_content
                    if is_mkdocs and clean_content.startswith("---"):
                        parts = clean_content.split("---", 2)
                        if len(parts) >= 3:
                            clean_content = parts[2].strip()

                    self.chapters_written_so_far.append(clean_content)

                    if cached_summary:
                        self.chapter_summaries.append(cached_summary)
                    else:
                        summary_prompt = build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num, abstraction_name, clean_content, language)
                        chapter_summary = call_llm(
                            summary_prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level
                        )
                        self.chapter_summaries.append(f"{get('UI_CHAPTER')} {chapter_num} — {abstraction_name.strip()}:\n{chapter_summary}")

                    summary_entry = self.chapter_summaries[-1] if self.chapter_summaries else None
                    return {"content": clean_content, "hash": current_hash, "name": abstraction_name, "summary": summary_entry}
        except Exception as e:
            emit("WARN_MANIFEST_CACHE_FAIL", error=e)

The first phase concatenates relevant code snippets into file_context_str. If incremental caching is active, it computes an MD5 checksum over this content and checks .doc_cache_manifest.json. On a cache hit, it loads the existing Markdown file, strips frontmatter if necessary, appends the cached summary (or regenerates it if missing), and returns early to skip redundant LLM inference.

docs.title: Phase 2: Rolling Summaries Context Budgeting
docs.text:
prev_chapters_budget = int(max_tokens * 0.50)

if self.chapter_summaries:
    selected_summaries = []
    running_tokens = 0

    # Build from newest to oldest — most recent chapters are most relevant
    for summary in reversed(self.chapter_summaries):
        summary_tokens = count_tokens(summary)
        if running_tokens + summary_tokens > prev_chapters_budget and selected_summaries:
            break
        selected_summaries.append(summary)
        running_tokens += summary_tokens

    selected_summaries.reverse()  # Restore chronological order

    if len(selected_summaries) < len(self.chapter_summaries):
        dropped = len(self.chapter_summaries) - len(selected_summaries)
        emit(
            "PREV_CHAPTERS_TRIMMED",
            dropped=dropped,
            total=len(self.chapter_summaries),
            budget=f"{prev_chapters_budget:,}",
            kept=len(selected_summaries),
        )
        window_note = f"[{dropped} earlier chapter summaries omitted — showing {len(selected_summaries)} most recent for context budget]"
        previous_chapters_summary = window_note + "\n---\n" + "\n---\n".join(selected_summaries)
    else:
        previous_chapters_summary = "\n---\n".join(self.chapter_summaries)
else:
    previous_chapters_summary = ""

The second phase manages context window usage for prior chapter summaries, capping their combined footprint at 50% of max_tokens. Summaries are accumulated from newest to oldest to preserve immediate contextual relevance. If older summaries exceed the budget, they are dropped and a notation is prepended to the remaining summaries.

The third phase builds language directives covering text translation, diagram localization, code comment preservation, and link target retention. It loads draft_chapters, interpolates all context variables, logs token usage breakdowns, and dispatches the drafting request through call_llm().

docs.title: Phase 4: Heading Normalization and Dynamic Summarization
docs.text:
response_tokens = count_tokens(chapter_content)
emit("DONE_WRITE_CHAPTER", chapter_num=chapter_num, tokens=f"{response_tokens:,}")

chapter_word = get("UI_CHAPTER")
actual_heading = f"# {chapter_word} {chapter_num}: {abstraction_name}"
if not chapter_content.strip().startswith(f"# {chapter_word} {chapter_num}") and mode != "api-reference":
    lines = chapter_content.strip().split("\n")
    if lines and lines[0].strip().startswith("#"):
        lines[0] = actual_heading
        chapter_content = "\n".join(lines)
    else:
        chapter_content = f"{actual_heading}\n\n{chapter_content}"

self.chapters_written_so_far.append(chapter_content)

# Generate LLM summary (used for cross-chapter context AND nav grouping)
summary_prompt = build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num, abstraction_name, chapter_content, language)
chapter_content_tokens = count_tokens(chapter_content)
summary_tokens = count_tokens(summary_prompt)
summary_overhead = summary_tokens - chapter_content_tokens
token_usage_summary = {
    "chapter_content": chapter_content_tokens,
    "overhead": summary_overhead,
}
emit("LLM_CALL_SUMMARIZE", chapter_num=chapter_num)
log_token_estimation("ChapterSummary", summary_prompt, max_tokens, token_usage=token_usage_summary)
chapter_summary = call_llm(summary_prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level)
summary_response_tokens = count_tokens(chapter_summary)
self.chapter_summaries.append(f"{get('UI_CHAPTER')} {chapter_num} — {abstraction_name.strip()}:\n{chapter_summary}")

summary_entry = f"{get('UI_CHAPTER')} {chapter_num} — {abstraction_name.strip()}:\n{chapter_summary}"
return {"content": chapter_content, "hash": current_hash, "name": abstraction_name, "summary": summary_entry}

The final phase normalizes the document's top-level header to match # Chapter N: Name (unless operating in API reference mode). It appends the draft to chapters_written_so_far, invokes call_llm() with a summary prompt to generate a 3-5 sentence brief of the chapter, appends the summary to chapter_summaries for subsequent chapters, and returns the chapter dictionary.

docs.title: WriteChapters.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: list[dict], exec_res_list: list[dict]) -> None:

Description: Persists drafted chapter contents to shared["chapters"], updates .doc_cache_manifest.json with hashes and summaries, saves chapter summaries for navigation grouping, and cleans up temporary instance state.

def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res_list):
    shared["chapters"] = [res["content"] for res in exec_res_list]

    if shared.get("incremental"):
        output_dir = os.path.join(shared.get("output_dir", "output"), shared.get("project_name"))
        os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
        manifest_path = os.path.join(output_dir, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")

        manifest = {}
        if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
            try:
                with open(manifest_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    manifest = json.load(f)
            except Exception:
                pass

        for res in exec_res_list:
            if res.get("hash") and res.get("name"):
                manifest[res["name"]] = {
                    "hash": res["hash"],
                    "summary": res.get("summary", ""),
                }

        with open(manifest_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2)

    shared["chapter_summaries"] = list(self.chapter_summaries)

    del self.chapters_written_so_far
    del self.chapter_summaries
    emit("DONE_ALL_CHAPTERS", count=len(exec_res_list))

The method extracts the Markdown text from each item in exec_res_list into shared["chapters"]. If incremental mode is enabled, it updates .doc_cache_manifest.json with current file hashes and summaries. It preserves chapter_summaries in shared for downstream navigation clustering in CombineTutorial, deletes instance-level tracking buffers, and emits completion telemetry.

docs.title: CombineTutorial.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> dict:

Description: Generates the architectural relationship Mermaid flowchart, handles module name disambiguation, builds the table of contents or MkDocs navigation tree, and injects YAML frontmatter.

docs.title: Phase 1: Mermaid Flowchart Construction
docs.text:
project_name = shared["project_name"]
output_base_dir = shared.get("output_dir", "output")
output_path = os.path.join(output_base_dir, project_name)
repo_url = shared.get("repo_url")
_language = shared.get("language", "english")

relationships_data = shared["relationships"]
chapter_order = shared["chapter_order"]
abstractions = shared["abstractions"]
chapters_content = shared["chapters"]

# --- Generate Mermaid Diagram ---
mermaid_lines = ["flowchart TD"]
for i, abstr in enumerate(abstractions):
    node_id = f"A{i}"
    sanitized_name = abstr["name"].replace('"', "").replace("\n", " ").strip()
    node_label = sanitized_name
    mermaid_lines.append(f'    {node_id}("{node_label}")')
for rel in relationships_data["details"]:
    from_node_id = f"A{rel['from']}"
    to_node_id = f"A{rel['to']}"
    edge_label = rel["label"].replace('"', "").replace("\n", " ")
    max_label_len = 30
    if len(edge_label) > max_label_len:
        edge_label = edge_label[: max_label_len - 3] + "..."
    mermaid_lines.append(f'    {from_node_id} -- "{edge_label}" --> {to_node_id}')

incoming = {f"A{i}": 0 for i in range(len(abstractions))}
for rel in relationships_data["details"]:
    incoming[f"A{rel['to']}"] += 1
entry_nodes = [nid for nid, inc in incoming.items() if inc >= 2]
if entry_nodes:
    mermaid_lines.append("    classDef entryNode stroke:#d33,stroke-width:3px,fill:#fff5f5")
    mermaid_lines.extend(f"    class {node_id} entryNode" for node_id in entry_nodes)

mermaid_diagram = "\n".join(mermaid_lines)

The first phase converts abstraction entities and relationships into a Mermaid flowchart TD definition. Edge labels exceeding 30 characters are truncated. In-degree counts are calculated across all nodes; nodes with two or more incoming edges are classified as foundation nodes and styled with the entryNode class (stroke:#d33,stroke-width:3px,fill:#fff5f5).

docs.title: Phase 2: MkDocs Navigation and Frontmatter Assembly
docs.text:
ui = {
    "tutorial": get("UI_TUTORIAL"),
    "source_repo": get("UI_SOURCE_REPO"),
    "chapters": get("UI_CHAPTERS"),
    "toc": get("UI_TOC"),
    "chapter": get("UI_CHAPTER"),
    "full_content": get("UI_FULL_CONTENT"),
}

is_mkdocs = shared.get("mkdocs", False)

if is_mkdocs:
    nav_items = []
    chapter_files = []

    for i, abstraction_index in enumerate(chapter_order):
        if 0 <= abstraction_index < len(abstractions) and i < len(chapters_content):
            abstraction_name = abstractions[abstraction_index]["name"].replace("\n", " ").strip()
            original_path = abstractions[abstraction_index].get("original_path")

            if original_path:
                doc_rel_path = original_path + ".md"
                filename = doc_rel_path.replace(os.sep, "/")
            else:
                safe_name = "".join(c if c.isalnum() else "_" for c in abstraction_name).lower()
                filename = f"{safe_name}.md"

            dir_prefix = os.path.dirname(original_path) if original_path else ""
            nav_items.append((dir_prefix, abstraction_name, filename))

            chapter_content = chapters_content[i]
            frontmatter = f"---\ntitle: {abstraction_name}\nsidebar_position: {i + 1}\n---\n\n"

            if not chapter_content.startswith("---"):
                chapter_content = frontmatter + chapter_content

            if not chapter_content.endswith("\n\n"):
                chapter_content += "\n\n"

            chapter_files.append(
                {
                    "filename": filename,
                    "content": chapter_content,
                    "module_name": abstraction_name,
                    "description": abstractions[abstraction_index].get("description", ""),
                    "original_path": abstractions[abstraction_index].get("original_path", ""),
                }
            )

    name_counts = Counter(cf["module_name"] for cf in chapter_files)
    for cf in chapter_files:
        if name_counts[cf["module_name"]] > 1 and cf.get("original_path"):
            dir_prefix = os.path.dirname(cf["original_path"])
            if dir_prefix:
                cf["module_name"] = f"{dir_prefix}/{cf['module_name']}"

When MkDocs mode is enabled, the second phase assigns relative file targets, prepends YAML frontmatter (title, sidebar_position) to each chapter, and packages entries into chapter_files. To prevent navigation conflicts, duplicate module names from different directories are disambiguated by prepending their parent directory path.

docs.text:
if is_mkdocs:
        # Build flat nav with directory sub-grouping
        dir_groups = defaultdict(list)
        for dir_prefix, nav_label, filename in nav_items:
            dir_groups[dir_prefix].append((nav_label, filename))

        nav_lines = ["    - api/index.md"]
        has_non_root = any(d for d in dir_groups)
        if has_non_root:
            for dir_path in sorted(dir_groups.keys()):
                if dir_path:
                    nav_lines.append(f"    - {dir_path}:")
                    for nav_label, filename in dir_groups[dir_path]:
                        nav_lines.append(f"      - '{nav_label}': 'api/{filename}'")
                else:
                    for nav_label, filename in dir_groups[dir_path]:
                        nav_lines.append(f"    - '{nav_label}': 'api/{filename}'")
        else:
            for _dir_prefix, nav_label, filename in nav_items:
                nav_lines.append(f"    - '{nav_label}': 'api/{filename}'")
        mode = shared.get("mode", "tutorial")
        nav_section = {
            "tutorial": get("UI_MODE_TUTORIAL"),
            "advanced": get("UI_MODE_ADVANCED"),
            "sdk": get("UI_MODE_SDK"),
            "api-reference": get("UI_MODE_API_REF"),
        }.get(mode, "Documentation")
        nav_snippet = f"nav:\n  - {nav_section}:\n" + "\n".join(nav_lines)

        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"CombineTutorial prep | is_mkdocs=True | chapters={len(chapter_files)}", dest="LOG")
        return {
            "output_path": output_path,
            "output_base_dir": output_base_dir,
            "is_mkdocs": True,
            "nav_snippet": nav_snippet,
            "chapter_files": chapter_files,
            "ui": ui,
            "project_name": project_name,
            "mode": shared.get("mode", "tutorial"),
            "chapter_summaries": shared.get("chapter_summaries", []),
            "directory_tree": shared.get("directory_tree", ""),
            "language": shared.get("language", "english"),
            "use_cache": shared.get("use_cache", True),
            "thinking_level": shared.get("thinking_level"),
            "max_tokens": shared.get("max_tokens", 100000),
        }

    # Traditional tutorial mode
    index_content = f"# {ui['tutorial']}: {project_name}\n\n"
    index_content += f"{relationships_data['summary']}\n\n"
    if repo_url:
        index_content += f"**{ui['source_repo']}:** [{repo_url}]({repo_url})\n\n"
    else:
        local_dir = shared.get("local_dir", "")
        if local_dir:
            index_content += f"**{ui['source_repo']}:** `{local_dir}`\n\n"

    index_content += "```mermaid\n"
    index_content += mermaid_diagram + "\n"
    index_content += "```\n\n"
    index_content += f"## {ui['chapters']}\n\n"

    chapter_files = []
    for i, abstraction_index in enumerate(chapter_order):
        if 0 <= abstraction_index < len(abstractions) and i < len(chapters_content):
            abstraction_name = abstractions[abstraction_index]["name"].replace("\n", " ").strip()
            safe_name = "".join(c if c.isalnum() else "_" for c in abstraction_name).lower()
            filename = f"{i + 1:02d}_{safe_name}.md"
            index_content += f"{i + 1}. [{abstraction_name}]({filename})\n"

            chapter_content = chapters_content[i]
            if not chapter_content.endswith("\n\n"):
                chapter_content += "\n\n"
            chapter_files.append({"filename": filename, "content": chapter_content})
        else:
            emit("WARN_CHAPTER_MISMATCH", index=i)

    index_content += f"\n---\n\n**{ui['full_content']}:** [full_content.md](full_content.md)\n"

    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"CombineTutorial prep | is_mkdocs={is_mkdocs} | chapters={len(chapter_files)}", dest="LOG")
    return {
        "output_path": output_path,
        "output_base_dir": output_base_dir,
        "is_mkdocs": False,
        "index_content": index_content,
        "chapter_files": chapter_files,
        "ui": ui,
    }

The third phase compiles the navigation payload. In MkDocs mode, it generates a fallback nav_snippet organized by directory. In standalone mode, it constructs index.md containing the project title, repository source, the Mermaid relationship diagram, a numbered table of contents linking to chapter files, and a reference to full_content.md.

docs.title: CombineTutorial.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: dict) -> str:

Description: Creates output directories and delegates site generation to write_mkdocs_output() or write_standalone_output().

@safe_exec
def exec(self, prep_res):
    output_path = prep_res["output_path"]
    is_mkdocs = prep_res["is_mkdocs"]
    chapter_files = prep_res["chapter_files"]
    ui = prep_res["ui"]

    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"NODE EXEC | node=CombineTutorial | action=write_output | output={output_path} | chapters={len(chapter_files)} | mkdocs={is_mkdocs}",
        dest="LOG",
    )
    emit("COMBINE_WRITING_OUTPUT", path=output_path)
    os.makedirs(output_path, exist_ok=True)

    if is_mkdocs:
        write_mkdocs_output(output_path, prep_res, chapter_files)
    else:
        write_standalone_output(output_path, prep_res, chapter_files, ui)

    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"NODE COMPLETE | node=CombineTutorial | output={output_path} | files_written={len(chapter_files) + 1}",
        dest="LOG",
    )
    return output_path

The method creates output_path using os.makedirs(exist_ok=True). It branches based on is_mkdocs, invoking write_mkdocs_output() to generate the MkDocs site (including YAML configuration, landing pages, and assets) or write_standalone_output() to write standalone Markdown files and aggregated full_content.md. It returns output_path.

docs.title: safe_exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Internal (Module-level decorator) Signature: def safe_exec(func: callable) -> callable:

Description: A decorator that wraps Node.exec() implementations with standardized error handling. When an unhandled exception occurs during node execution, the decorator catches the error, emits a localized NODE_RETRY_ERROR telemetry event, logs a diagnostic traceback to the session log sink via emit_raw(), and re-raises the exception to trigger the PocketFlow retry policy.

Parameters: * func (callable): The exec method of a Node or BatchNode instance.

Returns: * callable: The decorated wrapper function.

Raises: * Exception: Re-raises any exception thrown by func.

Example: 

# Extracted from safe_exec implementation in nodes.py
def safe_exec(func):
    @wraps(func)
    def wrapper(self, *args, **kwargs):
        try:
            return func(self, *args, **kwargs)
        except Exception as e:
            emit("NODE_RETRY_ERROR", class_name=self.__class__.__name__, error=e)
            emit_raw("ERROR", f"[Node {self.__class__.__name__}] Error: {e}\n{traceback.format_exc()}", dest="LOG")
            raise

    return wrapper

The helper eliminates duplicate try/except blocks across nodes, ensuring uniform telemetry logging while allowing PocketFlow's DAG engine to manage retry policies via max_retries and wait.

docs.title: create_llm_context()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (Closure scoped within IdentifyAbstractions.prep) Signature: def create_llm_context(files_data: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> str:

Description: Accumulates file contents into a single Markdown-formatted string, measuring token consumption per file and stopping if the safety limit (95% of max_tokens) is reached.

Parameters: * files_data (list[tuple[str, str]]): Ordered list of (filepath, content) tuples.

Returns: * str: The accumulated, token-bounded context string.

Example: 

# Extracted from IdentifyAbstractions.prep implementation in nodes.py
def create_llm_context(files_data):
    max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)

    safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)

    context = ""
    current_tokens = 0

    for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
        entry = f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"

        entry_tokens = count_tokens(entry)

        if current_tokens + entry_tokens > safety_limit:
            emit("WARN_CONTEXT_TRUNCATED", index=i, path=path, limit=safety_limit)
            break

        context += entry
        current_tokens += entry_tokens

    return context

The closure enforces context boundaries for small repositories. If adding a file would push total tokens past safety_limit, it emits a WARN_CONTEXT_TRUNCATED warning and breaks out of accumulation, protecting downstream LLM calls from context overflow.

docs.title: SharedStoreContext
docs.text:
The blackboard dictionary contract shared across all nodes in the PocketFlow DAG.

Field Type Description repo_url str \| None Remote GitHub repository URL if remote ingestion was requested. local_dir str \| None Local directory path if local ingestion was requested. project_name str Name of the project, derived from the repository URL or directory name. github_token str \| None Personal access token used for authenticated GitHub API crawling. include_patterns list[str] Glob patterns specifying files to include during crawling. exclude_patterns list[str] \| set[str] Glob patterns specifying files to exclude during crawling. max_file_size int Maximum file size in bytes for ingested source files. files list[tuple[str, str]] Ingested repository files formatted as (relative_path, file_content) tuples. max_tokens int Operational token ceiling resolved for the current model. force_batch bool Flag that forces batching even when total tokens fit within the model limit. batch_size int Maximum number of files permitted within a single batch (default: 50). file_batches list[list[tuple]] Grouped file batches assembled by ContextRouter. directory_tree str Multiline hierarchical directory tree string. mapped_abstractions list[dict] Partial abstraction objects discovered across batches by MapAbstractions. abstractions list[dict] Consolidated abstraction records defining the documentation chapters. relationships dict Architectural relationships dictionary containing summary and details. chapter_order list[int] Sequence of abstraction indices defining the chapter reading order. chapters list[str] Generated Markdown text for all chapters. chapter_summaries list[str] LLM-generated technical summaries of each chapter. final_output_dir str Absolute filesystem path where generated artifacts were written.

Example:

Field Type Description hash str MD5 hexadecimal digest of the chapter's input source file snippets. summary str Cached chapter summary used for cross-chapter context in subsequent runs.

Example: 

{
  "call_llm.py": {
    "hash": "4f53cda18c2baa0c0354bb5f9a3ecbe9",
    "summary": "Chapter 1 — call_llm.py:\nThe call_llm.py module serves as the centralized inference gateway..."
  }
}

docs.title: Exception Interception via @safe_exec
docs.text: All LLM-facing exec() methods use the @safe_exec decorator. When an exception occurs during prompt execution or response parsing: 1. It emits a localized NODE_RETRY_ERROR event via emit() containing the node class name and exception message. 2. It logs a full stack trace to the persistent session log file via emit_raw(..., dest="LOG"). 3. It re-raises the exception to trigger PocketFlow's configured retry policy (max_retries=5, wait=20).

docs.title: Ingestion Validation
docs.text:
In FetchRepo.exec(), empty file sets trigger an unrecoverable failure: 

if len(files_list) == 0:
    raise ValueError("No matching files found. Check your directory and include/exclude patterns.")
This fails fast if invalid glob patterns or empty directories are supplied, preventing downstream nodes from executing on empty inputs.

docs.title: Defensive Model Output Validation
docs.text: Nodes that deserialize LLM YAML responses implement strict structural checks: * IdentifyAbstractions.exec(): Verifies that the deserialized payload is a list of dictionaries with name, description, and file_indices keys. It validates string types and handles index strings, comments, and hyphenated ranges (e.g., 1-4), logging WARN_PARSE_INDEX and skipping invalid entries. * AnalyzeRelationships.exec(): Validates that relationships_data contains summary and relationships keys. It extracts integers from index strings via re.findall(r"\d+", ...), confirms both endpoints fall within [0, num_abstractions - 1], and emits WARN_INVALID_RELATIONSHIP for out-of-bounds references. * OrderChapters.exec(): Validates that the returned list forms a permutation of all abstraction indices. If an index is out of bounds, contains duplicates, or omits abstractions (len(ordered_indices) != num_abstractions), it raises a ValueError to trigger node retry.

docs.title: Manifest and Cache Fault Tolerance
docs.text: In WriteChapters.exec(), all interactions with .doc_cache_manifest.json are enclosed in try...except Exception as e: blocks. If the manifest file is corrupted, unreadable, or contains invalid JSON: 1. It emits a WARN_MANIFEST_CACHE_FAIL warning. 2. It falls back to clean LLM drafting without halting execution.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The call_llm.py module serves as the primary inference gateway for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder framework. It abstracts multi-provider Large Language Model (LLM) communications behind a unified interface, decoupling pipeline execution stages from underlying inference protocol details. The module supports direct integrations with Google Gemini (via both Google GenAI Client and Vertex AI) as well as OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints, specifically accommodating providers such as OpenRouter and local Ollama instances.

In addition to standard request routing, the module encapsulates caching and reasoning effort orchestration. Prompt-response cycles are optionally memoized to a persistent JSON-backed cache file (llm_cache.json), supported by an in-memory singleton that prevents redundant filesystem reads across multiple pipeline tasks. When reasoning-capable models are targeted, call_llm.py parses and translates thinking effort levels (low, medium, high) into provider-native configuration constructs, including Gemini thinking token budgets and OpenRouter/Ollama reasoning parameter payloads.

The following architectural flowchart illustrates the runtime request path, demonstrating cache evaluation, token auditing, provider resolution, and execution handling across the supported provider interfaces:

docs.title: call_llm()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Executes an inference call using the resolved active provider, providing token auditing, timing metrics, and optional persistent caching. Under the hood, this function manages four distinct logical phases: inspecting execution parameters, querying the in-memory/disk cache, dynamically routing execution to either the native Gemini client or the OpenAI-compatible HTTP wrapper, and committing newly generated responses back to the cache store.

docs.title: Phase 1: Token Profiling and Execution Logging
docs.text:
from utils.output import emit, emit_raw
    from utils.token_utils import count_tokens

    provider = get_llm_provider()
    model = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_MODEL", os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL", "unknown"))
    prompt_tokens = count_tokens(prompt)

    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"{'=' * 80}", dest="LOG")
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"LLM CALL START | provider={provider} | model={model} | thinking={thinking_level} | cache={'enabled' if use_cache else 'disabled'} | prompt_tokens={prompt_tokens:,}",
        dest="LOG",
    )
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"PROMPT:\n{prompt}", dest="LOG")
This phase identifies the target provider using get_llm_provider() imported from utils/llm_config.py and extracts the active model identifier from the corresponding environment variable. The raw prompt token consumption is calculated using count_tokens() from utils/token_utils.py. Detailed operational metadata—including model name, reasoning mode, cache settings, and full prompt contents—is emitted to the log destination using emit_raw() from utils/output.py.

docs.title: Phase 2: Cache Evaluation and Hit Return
docs.text:
# Check cache if enabled
    if use_cache:
        cache = load_cache()
        if prompt in cache:
            cached_response = cache[prompt]
            emit("CACHE_HIT", chars=f"{len(cached_response):,}")
            emit_raw("DEBUG", f"RESPONSE (cached):\n{cached_response}", dest="LOG")
            emit_raw("DEBUG", "LLM CALL END | result=cache_hit", dest="LOG")
            return cached_response
        emit("CACHE_MISS")
When caching is enabled, the function calls load_cache() to obtain the cache dictionary. If an exact match for the raw prompt string exists within the cache keys, the function short-circuits execution immediately. It emits a CACHE_HIT event indicating character count, logs the complete cached text, and returns the response without dispatching any network operations. If the prompt does not exist in the store, a CACHE_MISS notification is emitted.

docs.title: Phase 3: Execution Dispatch and Latency Tracking
docs.text:
# Make the actual LLM call
    start_time = time.time()
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"API CALL | sending request to {provider}...", dest="LOG")

    if provider == "GEMINI":
        response_text = _call_llm_gemini(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
    else:  # generic method using a URL that is OpenAI compatible API (Ollama, ...)
        response_text = _call_llm_provider(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)

    elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"API CALL COMPLETE | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | response_chars={len(response_text):,}", dest="LOG")
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"RESPONSE:\n{response_text}", dest="LOG")
If execution proceeds past cache lookup, high-precision timing begins via time.time(). Depending on the provider resolved from the environment, execution branches to _call_llm_gemini() for Google's native SDK or _call_llm_provider() for OpenAI-compatible HTTP providers like OpenRouter and Ollama. Upon completion, total elapsed wall-clock time and response string lengths are calculated and logged alongside the raw output.

docs.title: Phase 4: Cache Update and Return
docs.text:
# Update cache if enabled
    if use_cache:
        cache = load_cache()
        cache[prompt] = response_text
        save_cache(cache)
        emit_raw("DEBUG", "CACHE WRITE | saved response to cache", dest="LOG")

    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"LLM CALL END | result=success | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s", dest="LOG")
    return response_text
Following a successful API call, if use_cache is set to True, the returned text is associated with the original prompt in the cache dictionary. The modified structure is written to disk via save_cache(), persisting the state across subsequent process runs. Finally, an operational completion event is logged, and the generated text is returned to the caller.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The complete input prompt text submitted for inference. * use_cache (bool): Flag determining whether to query and write to the local memoization cache (llm_cache.json). Defaults to True. * thinking_level (str | None): Optional reasoning depth identifier ("low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The textual response generated by the resolved model.

Raises: * ValueError: If required environment variables are absent, if the provider returns invalid JSON, or if the response lacks valid output structures. * Exception: Wrapped connection errors, timeouts, or HTTP failures returned during network communication.

Example: 

if __name__ == "__main__":
    from utils.output import emit

    test_prompt = "Hello, how are you?"

    emit("SELFTEST_LLM_CALL")
    response1 = call_llm(test_prompt, use_cache=False)
    emit("SELFTEST_LLM_RESPONSE", response=response1)

docs.title: load_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def load_cache() -> dict:

Description: Retrieves the memoization dictionary from the module-level singleton variable _cache, populating it from disk on initial invocation. By caching the parsed dictionary in memory, subsequent invocations avoid reparsing potentially massive JSON files on every inference step. If the cache file does not exist, contains corrupted JSON, or cannot be accessed due to OS permissions, the error is logged and an empty dictionary is initialized.

def load_cache():
    global _cache
    if _cache is not None:
        return _cache
    try:
        with open(cache_file) as f:
            _cache = json.load(f)
        from utils.output import emit

        emit("CACHE_LOADED", count=f"{len(_cache):,}", file=cache_file)
    except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError, OSError) as e:
        from utils.output import emit, emit_raw

        emit("WARN_CACHE_LOAD_FAIL")
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Cache load error: {e}", dest="LOG")
        _cache = {}
    return _cache
The implementation uses a global reference _cache to store the loaded dictionary. If _cache already holds an object, it is returned immediately without filesystem I/O. If not yet initialized, it reads from cache_file (llm_cache.json) and parses it using json.load. On success, it emits CACHE_LOADED with the count of cached items. If disk reading encounters FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError, or OSError, it falls back to an empty dictionary {} while notifying through emit() and emit_raw().

Parameters: None.

Returns: * dict: In-memory dictionary containing prompt-to-response key-value mappings.

Raises: None directly. Filesystem and parsing exceptions are intercepted and handled with fallbacks.

Example: 

# Extracted from call_llm() implementation
if use_cache:
    cache = load_cache()
    if prompt in cache:
        cached_response = cache[prompt]

docs.title: save_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def save_cache(cache: dict) -> None:

Description: Persists the current in-memory cache dictionary to disk at the path defined by cache_file (llm_cache.json), while updating the internal singleton pointer. Serializes the entire dictionary structure into JSON format. If disk writing fails due to permission restrictions, missing storage mounts, or un-serializable objects, the function traps the exception and emits diagnostic warnings without interrupting pipeline flow.

def save_cache(cache):
    global _cache
    _cache = cache
    try:
        with open(cache_file, "w") as f:
            json.dump(cache, f)
    except (OSError, TypeError) as e:
        from utils.output import emit, emit_raw

        emit("WARN_CACHE_SAVE_FAIL")
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Cache save error: {e}", dest="LOG")
The function takes the modified cache mapping, reassigns the module-level _cache reference, and opens cache_file for writing. It uses json.dump() to serialize the dictionary to disk. Any OSError (e.g., read-only filesystem, disk full) or TypeError (e.g., unhashable or non-serializable payload) is caught to prevent unhandled exceptions from terminating long-running pipeline batches. Failures trigger emission of WARN_CACHE_SAVE_FAIL alongside raw log traces.

Parameters: * cache (dict): The dictionary of prompts and responses to be persisted.

Returns: * None

Raises: None directly. Traps OSError and TypeError.

Example: 

# Extracted from call_llm() implementation
if use_cache:
    cache = load_cache()
    cache[prompt] = response_text
    save_cache(cache)
    emit_raw("DEBUG", "CACHE WRITE | saved response to cache", dest="LOG")

docs.title: _call_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Constructs and dispatches standard HTTP requests targeting OpenAI-compatible completions endpoints (such as OpenRouter or Ollama). It parses provider-specific environment variables, injects reasoning configurations, posts JSON payloads with defensive timeouts, and validates response schema structures.

docs.title: Phase 1: Environment Configuration and Validation
docs.text:
# Read the provider from environment variable
    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if not provider:
        raise ValueError("LLM_PROVIDER environment variable is required")

    # Construct the names of the other environment variables
    model_var = f"{provider}_MODEL"
    base_url_var = f"{provider}_BASE_URL"
    api_key_var = f"{provider}_API_KEY"

    # Read the provider-specific variables
    model = os.environ.get(model_var)
    base_url = os.environ.get(base_url_var)
    api_key = os.environ.get(api_key_var, "")  # API key is optional, default to empty string

    # Validate required variables
    if not model:
        raise ValueError(f"{model_var} environment variable is required")
    if not base_url:
        raise ValueError(f"{base_url_var} environment variable is required")

    # Append the endpoint to the base URL
    url = f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}/v1/chat/completions"
This phase retrieves the provider designation from LLM_PROVIDER and constructs dynamic variable keys for model, base URL, and API key. It strictly validates that both the model identifier and base URL are present, raising a ValueError if either is missing. It formats the target endpoint by stripping trailing slashes from the base URL and appending /v1/chat/completions.

docs.title: Phase 2: Reasoning and Payload Construction
docs.text:
# Configure headers and payload based on provider
    headers = {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
    }
    if api_key:  # Only add Authorization header if API key is provided
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"

    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        "temperature": 0.7,
    }

    if provider == "OPENROUTER" and thinking_level:
        model_info = _get_openrouter_model_info(model)
        if model_info and "reasoning" in model_info:
            supported_efforts = model_info["reasoning"].get("supported_efforts", [])
            if thinking_level.lower() in supported_efforts:
                payload["reasoning"] = {"effort": thinking_level.lower()}
                payload["temperature"] = 1.0  # Required for many reasoning models
            else:
                from utils.output import emit

                emit("WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_INVALID", level=thinking_level, model=model, supported=str(supported_efforts))
        else:
            from utils.output import emit

            emit("WARN_THINKING_NOT_SUPPORTED", model=model)

    elif provider == "OLLAMA" and thinking_level:
        # Some Ollama SDKs / API versions look for `think`, others look for standard `reasoning_effort`
        payload["think"] = thinking_level.lower()
        payload["reasoning_effort"] = thinking_level.lower()
        payload["temperature"] = 1.0
This phase builds the standard JSON payload and HTTP headers. If an API key is available, an Authorization: Bearer <token> header is added. When thinking_level is requested for OpenRouter, the helper queries _get_openrouter_model_info() from utils/llm_config.py to verify whether the model advertises reasoning effort support, setting payload["reasoning"] = {"effort": ...} and raising temperature to 1.0 when verified. For Ollama, both think and reasoning_effort payload fields are populated to ensure compatibility across disparate Ollama runtime releases.

docs.title: Phase 3: HTTP Request Execution and Response Validation
docs.text:
try:
        response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=(10, 300))
        try:
            response_json = response.json()  # Log the response
        except (ValueError, requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError):
            from utils.output import emit

            emit(
                "WARN_INVALID_JSON",
                status_code=response.status_code,
                preview=response.text[:200].strip(),
            )
            raise ValueError(f"Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}") from None
        response.raise_for_status()

        # Defensive check: API may return 200 with error/rate-limit payload missing 'choices'
        if "choices" not in response_json or not response_json["choices"]:
            error_detail = response_json.get("error", response_json)
            from utils.output import emit

            emit("WARN_API_NO_CHOICES", detail=str(error_detail))
            raise ValueError(f"API response missing 'choices' key. Response: {error_detail}")

        return response_json["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
The HTTP request is executed via requests.post() with a connect timeout of 10 seconds and read timeout of 300 seconds. The returned body is parsed into JSON, raising a detailed ValueError if the content fails JSON decoding. The helper invokes response.raise_for_status() to flag 4xx and 5xx HTTP codes. Crucially, a defensive check is performed to catch rate limits or provider-level errors that return HTTP 200 without a choices array, extracting and raising the nested error before accessing response_json["choices"][0]["message"]["content"].

docs.title: Phase 4: Network and Protocol Exception Translation
docs.text:
except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as e:
        error_message = f"HTTP error occurred: {e}"
        try:
            error_details = response.json().get("error", "No additional details")
            error_message += f" (Details: {error_details})"
        except Exception:
            pass
        raise Exception(error_message) from e
    except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to connect to {provider} API. Check your network connection.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.Timeout as e:
        raise Exception(f"Request to {provider} API timed out.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
        raise Exception(f"An error occurred while making the request to {provider}: {e}") from e
    except ValueError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to parse response as JSON from {provider}. The server might have returned an invalid response.") from e
Any lower-level exceptions occurring within the communication lifecycle are intercepted and transformed into descriptive pipeline-level exceptions. HTTP errors attempt to extract and append structured error payloads from the server response. Explicit handlers distinguish between socket connection failures, request timeouts, general request exceptions, and payload parsing errors, ensuring root causes are contextualized with the provider's identity.

Parameters: * prompt (str): Raw prompt string sent to the chat completions API. * thinking_level (str | None): Optional reasoning effort configuration string.

Returns: * str: Text content generated in message.content within the first completion choice.

Raises: * ValueError: If required environment variables are unset or response JSON lacks expected keys. * Exception: Normalized exception wrapping underlying requests errors.

Example: 

# Real usage extracted from call_llm()
if provider == "GEMINI":
    response_text = _call_llm_gemini(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
else:  # generic method using a URL that is OpenAI compatible API (Ollama, ...)
    response_text = _call_llm_provider(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)

docs.title: _call_llm_gemini()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Executes inference against Google Gemini models using the modern google.genai SDK. Discovers credentials dynamically to support both Vertex AI enterprise environments and Google AI Studio API key access, configures reasoning budgets, and strips non-text artifacts from multi-part response structures.

docs.title: Phase 1: Authentication and Client Initialization
docs.text:
if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
        client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"), location=os.getenv("GEMINI_LOCATION", "us-central1"))
    elif os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
        client = genai.Client(api_key=os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"))
    else:
        raise ValueError("Either GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY must be set in the environment")
    model = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.7-flash")

    kwargs = {"model": model, "contents": [prompt]}
This phase handles authentication resolution. If GEMINI_PROJECT_ID is present, the SDK client is initialized in Vertex AI mode with region fallback to us-central1. Otherwise, if GEMINI_API_KEY is present, standard API key authentication is selected. If neither is available, a ValueError is raised. The target model defaults to gemini-3.7-flash if GEMINI_MODEL is omitted, and the parameter dictionary kwargs is constructed.

docs.title: Phase 2: Thinking Budget and Generation Configuration
docs.text:
if thinking_level:
        # Map string levels to budgets for the installed SDK version
        budget_map = {"low": 1024, "medium": 4096, "high": 8192}
        budget = budget_map.get(thinking_level.lower(), 4096)
        from utils.output import emit_raw

        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"Gemini thinking config | budget={budget}", dest="LOG")
        thinking_config = types.ThinkingConfig(include_thoughts=True, thinking_budget=budget)
        kwargs["config"] = types.GenerateContentConfig(thinking_config=thinking_config)
When thinking_level is specified, string identifiers are converted into concrete integer token budgets using an internal mapping: low maps to 1024, medium to 4096, and high to 8192 tokens (defaulting to 4096 for unrecognized strings). A types.ThinkingConfig instance is created with include_thoughts=True and assigned to types.GenerateContentConfig, which is injected into the call's keyword arguments.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements layered fault-tolerance patterns designed to keep documentation generation pipelines operational despite transient networking failures, malformed remote payloads, or localized cache corruption:

  • Graceful Cache Degradation: In load_cache(), failures caused by missing files (FileNotFoundError), corrupt JSON (json.JSONDecodeError), or OS-level access issues (OSError) do not raise exceptions to the caller. Instead, the module logs a warning via emit("WARN_CACHE_LOAD_FAIL") and falls back to an empty dictionary {}. Similarly, save_cache() catches OSError and TypeError, preventing disk serialization issues from crashing active pipeline jobs.
  • Missing Provider Credentials Validation: Before any network operation is attempted, _call_llm_provider() and _call_llm_gemini() validate environment variables. If required settings (such as LLM_PROVIDER, <provider>_MODEL, or Gemini authentication keys) are missing, a descriptive ValueError is raised immediately.
  • Defensive HTTP Response Parsing: Providers returning status code 200 with non-JSON bodies or missing choices blocks (a pattern observed during upstream rate-limiting or provider error states) are caught. _call_llm_provider() explicitly verifies the existence and non-emptiness of response_json["choices"], raising a ValueError with embedded diagnostic details if the structure is invalid.
  • Network Exception Normalization: requests.exceptions.HTTPError, requests.exceptions.ConnectionError, and requests.exceptions.Timeout are caught and re-raised as standardized Exception instances with actionable troubleshooting advice (e.g., checking network connections or inspecting server error details).
  • Gemini Multi-Part Safety: To avoid runtime warnings when reasoning models include non-text artifacts (such as thought_signature), _call_llm_gemini() filters candidate parts via part.text is not None, ensuring only valid strings are concatenated.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Following the inference abstraction layer established in call_llm.py, which coordinates LLM queries and token budgeting, crawl_github_files.py acts as the primary remote ingestion engine for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder architecture. While local repositories are ingested through direct filesystem reads, remote targets require resilient retrieval mechanisms capable of traversing arbitrary Git trees, honoring repository ignore rules, parsing diverse Git reference specifications, and handling network or rate-limiting constraints. This module abstracts these challenges by providing a unified extraction interface that converts remote GitHub repositories into an in-memory dictionary of relative file paths and string contents.

The module operates across two distinct operational pipelines selected dynamically based on the repository URL schema: an SSH shallow clone pipeline and a GitHub REST API v3 traversal pipeline. When an SSH URL (prefixed with git@ or suffixed with .git) is supplied, the module provisions an isolated temporary directory via Python's tempfile module, invokes GitPython (git.Repo.clone_from) to clone the working tree, loads .gitignore rules using pathspec, and performs a filtered breadth-first filesystem walk. Conversely, when an HTTPS GitHub URL is supplied, the module parses the owner, repository, commit SHA, or branch reference from the URI path, queries the GitHub Contents and Git Trees REST APIs, downloads files directly via raw blob endpoints or decodes Base64 payloads, and handles API rate-limit resets with exponential or header-derived backoff delays.

Both pipelines converge on a common filtering and sanitization engine. Files and directories are matched against user-defined wildcard patterns (fnmatch) and Git-native .gitignore specifications (pathspec.PathSpec). The engine enforces strict file-size thresholds (defaulting to 1 MB) to prevent out-of-memory errors on massive assets, isolates binary artifacts by intercepting UTF-8 decoding failures, and standardizes progress telemetry via the centralized logging facilities in output.py. The final artifact is an ingested file mapping ready for downstream token profiling, document chunking, and LLM-driven architectural analysis.

docs.title: crawl_github_files()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def crawl_github_files(repo_url, token=None, max_file_size: int = DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE, use_relative_paths: bool = False, include_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None, exclude_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None) -> dict:

Description: Orchestrates the retrieval of source code files from a remote GitHub repository at a target commit, branch, or subpath. The function normalizes pattern configurations, evaluates the connection protocol, and executes either a local Git clone workflow or a recursive GitHub REST API crawler. It filters entries through size caps, Git wildmatch rules, and file name matchers while recording statistics for logging.

Parameters: * repo_url (str): Target repository URL. Supports SSH clone syntax (git@github.com:... or URLs ending in .git) and standard HTTPS tree URLs (e.g., https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/branch/subpath). * token (str, optional): GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT). Required for private repositories and recommended for public repositories to elevate GitHub API rate limits from 60 to 5,000 requests per hour. * max_file_size (int, optional): Maximum allowed size in bytes for downloaded source files. Defaults to 1_048_576 (1 MB). * use_relative_paths (bool, optional): When True, modifies keys in the returned file mapping to be relative to the queried subdirectory rather than the repository root. Defaults to False. * include_patterns (str | set[str] | None, optional): Glob pattern or set of glob patterns indicating which files must be included (e.g., "*.py" or {"*.md", "*.txt"}). If None, includes all files. * exclude_patterns (str | set[str] | None, optional): Glob pattern or set of glob patterns designating paths or filenames that must be omitted from ingestion.

Returns: * dict: Ingestion payload containing two root keys: "files", mapping string file paths to their decoded string contents, and "stats", tracking metrics such as total crawled items, skipped entries, and configuration metadata.

Raises: * ValueError: Raised when an HTTPS GitHub URL does not contain at least two path segments (owner and repo). * Exception: Raised when GitHub API rate limits are exhausted and no authentication token is provided to facilitate recovery.

docs.title: Phase 1: Parameter Normalization and Pattern Preprocessing
docs.text:
# Convert single pattern to set
    if include_patterns and isinstance(include_patterns, str):
        include_patterns = {include_patterns}
    if exclude_patterns and isinstance(exclude_patterns, str):
        exclude_patterns = {exclude_patterns}

    def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:
        """Determine if a file should be included based on patterns"""
        # If no include patterns are specified, include all files
        if not include_patterns:
            include_file = True
        else:
            # Check if file matches any include pattern
            include_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_name, pattern) for pattern in include_patterns)

        # Check gitignore if provided
        if include_file and gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path):
            return False

        # If exclude patterns are specified, check if file should be excluded
        if exclude_patterns and include_file:
            # Exclude if file matches any exclude pattern
            exclude_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_path, pattern) for pattern in exclude_patterns)
            return not exclude_file

        return include_file
The ingestion process begins by sanitizing string-based pattern parameters into Python set collections to ensure consistent iterable processing during pattern checks. The closure should_include_file is defined to encapsulate matching logic across both traversal pipelines. It sequentially validates whether a given file matches explicit inclusion filters, evaluates path compliance against compiled .gitignore rules via pathspec, and checks negative assertions defined by exclude_patterns.

docs.title: Phase 2: Protocol Discrimination and URL Routing
docs.text:
# Detect SSH URL (git@ or .git suffix)
    is_ssh_url = repo_url.startswith("git@") or repo_url.endswith(".git")

    if is_ssh_url:
        # Clone repo via SSH to temp dir
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdirname:
            emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"Cloning SSH repo {repo_url} to temp dir {tmpdirname} ...")
            try:
                repo = git.Repo.clone_from(repo_url, tmpdirname)
            except Exception as e:
                emit_raw("ERROR", f"Error cloning repo: {e}")
                return {"files": {}, "stats": {"error": str(e)}}
            # ...
The orchestrator checks the URI structure to determine whether to run an SSH-based clone or an HTTPS REST API crawler. If the URL begins with git@ or ends with .git, the system initializes a managed context using tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(). Within this temporary directory, it executes git.Repo.clone_from(repo_url, tmpdirname). Any low-level Git failures (such as authentication refusals or host key rejections) are intercepted, logged via emit_raw, and converted into an error dictionary response.

docs.title: Phase 3: SSH Working Tree Traversal and Ignore Rule Compilation
docs.text:
# Walk directory
            files = {}

            # --- Counters ---
            count_processed = 0
            count_excluded = 0
            count_size_limit = 0
            count_non_text = 0
            skipped_size_list = []
            skipped_non_text_list = []
            entry_num = 0

            # --- Load .gitignore ---
            gitignore_path = os.path.join(tmpdirname, ".gitignore")

                        gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", f.readlines())

Once the repository clone succeeds, the SSH pipeline initializes metric counters and attempts to read .gitignore from the root of the temporary checkout directory. If the file is present, it parses the ignore rules into a pathspec.PathSpec instance using the gitwildmatch standard, enabling standard Git wildcard resolution. Read failures or missing files degrade gracefully to None without blocking traversal.

docs.title: Phase 4: Directory Pruning and Local Filesystem Filtering
docs.text:
for root, dirs, filenames in os.walk(tmpdirname):
                # Filter directories
                excluded_dirs = set()
                for d in sorted(dirs):
                    dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), tmpdirname)
                    reason = None
                    if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
                        reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_GITIGNORE")
                    elif exclude_patterns:
                        for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                            dir_pattern = pattern.removesuffix("/*")
                            if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                                reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_EXCLUDED")
                                break

                    if reason:
                        excluded_dirs.add(d)
                        entry_num += 1
                        count_excluded += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_DIR_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=dirpath_rel, reason=reason)

                for d in dirs.copy():
                    if d in excluded_dirs:
                        dirs.remove(d)

                # Sort remaining dirs for consistent traversal order
                dirs.sort()
Directory scanning relies on os.walk(tmpdirname). To optimize traversal, directories are pruned in place by modifying dirs directly before recursing into subdirectories. Each directory candidate is checked against the parsed gitignore_spec and user-defined exclude_patterns. Any matched directory is tracked in excluded_dirs, logged via emit("CRAWL_DIR_EXCLUDED"), and removed from dirs to prevent unnecessary filesystem overhead in ignored subtrees.

docs.title: Phase 5: Local File Reading and Content Decoding
docs.text:
for filename in sorted(filenames):
                    abs_path = os.path.join(root, filename)
                    rel_path = os.path.relpath(abs_path, tmpdirname)
                    entry_num += 1

                    # Check include/exclude patterns
                    if not should_include_file(rel_path, filename, gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
                        count_excluded += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                        continue

                    # Check file size
                    try:
                        file_size = os.path.getsize(abs_path)
                    except OSError:
                        continue

                    if file_size > max_file_size:
                        count_size_limit += 1
                        skipped_size_list.append(rel_path)
                        size_kb = file_size / 1024
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                        continue

                    # Read content
                    try:
                        with open(abs_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                            content = f.read()
                        files[rel_path] = content
                        count_processed += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                        count_non_text += 1
                        skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    except Exception as e:
                        count_non_text += 1
                        skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_ERROR", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, error=e)
Files located within retained directories are sorted alphabetically for deterministic ordering. Each file is validated via should_include_file() and checked against max_file_size using os.path.getsize(). Qualifying files are opened with UTF-8 byte-order-mark support (utf-8-sig). Files containing binary data or invalid character encodings throw UnicodeDecodeError or ValueError, which are caught to mark the file as non-text, log the event, and preserve engine stability.
